universities.name: Università degli Studi di Genova
universities.research_summary: Genoa's ten legacy course leads now have official 2026/27 profiles and course-specific admission guidance. Computer Science BSc and Business Administration BSc are Italian-taught; English Computer Engineering BSc is at Imperia, while Energy Engineering MSc is at Savona. The 2027/28 visa preselection is expected from mid-December 2026 to end-March 2027, with €30 for up to two assessments and exact dates still pending. This university-level notice does not verify individual course intakes. The 2026/27 €136 initial tuition installment excludes the variable contribution and any regional-tax adjustment; ALiSEO awards require annual economic, enrollment and merit eligibility. No individual 2027/28 offer or new fee/scholarship call was identified for these ten leads. The separate Maritime non-offer notice and planned CORES status remain recorded.

source_urls.title: UniGeApply International Admissions
source_urls.evidence: 2027/28 non-EU visa preselection is expected mid-December 2026 through end-March 2027; exact dates await publication. €30 fee covers up to two assessment applications. English-taught programs do not require Italian.

source_urls.title: Maritime Science and Technology – degree programme not offered in 2027/28
source_urls.evidence: UniGe notice dated 18 September 2026 explicitly says the BSc Maritime Science and Technology will not be offered for 2027/28 and first-year enrollment will not be possible in that academic year.

source_urls.title: CORES Joint Master Degree – planned 2027/28 start
source_urls.evidence: UniGe announced the joint Master’s degree Conservation and Restoration Sciences (CORES), coordinated by UniGe with four European partner universities, with admissions planned to open in early 2027 and a planned start in academic year 2027/28. The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master proposal was still under evaluation, so formal approval, call terms and exact dates were not yet confirmed.

source_urls.title: UniGe degree course catalogue
source_urls.evidence: The catalogue links the ten reviewed BSc/MSc candidates to course profiles displaying Info 2026/2027. Separate Computer Engineering BSc records exist for Italian teaching in Genoa (11880) and English teaching in Imperia (12133). No named 2027/28 first-year offer is established by this catalogue.

source_urls.title: UniGeApply international admissions 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: For non-Italian qualifications, UniGeApply was the initial assessment route. Visa applicants: 26 November 2025–20 March 2026, €30 fixed for up to two requests; Computer Engineering BSc closed early on 8 March 2026. Resident selection opened 9 April 2026 and closed 28 August for MSc or 25 September for BSc, subject to restricted-course exceptions, and was free. Successful visa candidates continued via Universitaly. These are 2026/27 dates only.

source_urls.title: How tuition fees work – 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: Three installments: initial €136 consists of €16 stamp and €120 minimum regional tax, with any tax adjustment later. University contribution depends on ISEE-U, fee class, study group and full/part-time enrollment; the full-time table ranges from €0 to €3,300 plus fixed charges. 2026/27 deadlines: first installment 5 October for BSc or 30 November for open-access MSc, second 10 December 2026, third 23 June 2027. €136 is not total annual tuition.

source_urls.title: ISEE-University and equivalent ISEE – 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: For 2026/27, income-based fees use ISEE-U; eligible foreign household-income cases use equivalent ISEE-U parificato. Ordinary DSU/self-certification deadline is 31 October 2026. The page gives late DSU charges of €100 through 30 November and €200 from 1 December through 15 June 2027. Verify annual documentation and eligibility rather than assuming the lowest tuition bracket.

source_urls.title: UniGe university fee benefits
source_urls.evidence: Current guidance describes a €200 first-year contribution reduction for the highest entry-qualification mark and later-year merit reductions of €400 or €200, subject to the fee regulations. ALiSEO scholarship winners have university contribution and regional-tax exemptions. These rules do not establish a new 2027/28 scholarship call.

source_urls.title: ALiSEO scholarship and accommodation call 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: Annual competitive benefits require enrollment, merit and economic eligibility; ISEE/ISEEUP must not exceed €28,339 and ISPEU/ISPEUP €61,608. Awards vary by income band and on-site/commuting/off-site classification, with cash, meal and possible housing components. In band 1A an off-site housing applicant's €7,172 gross award includes services rather than all cash. Foreign-income applicants require the call's equivalent-ISEE documentation. No 2027/28 award is inferred.

source_urls.title: ALiSEO 2026/27 call instructions
source_urls.evidence: The 2026/27 scholarship/housing application window was 15 June–31 July 2026 at 12:00. The page says the deadline has passed. Foreign applicants without an Italian identity document have a separate registration procedure. This is a closed prior-cycle competition.

source_urls.title: UniGe Welcome Office – international students
source_urls.evidence: The Welcome Office contact is sass@unige.it; call centre 010 33 55 000, dial 4. The page links international-enrollment, support and appointment services. It also describes targeted 2026/27 Palestinian-student scholarships; these are not general international awards.

source_urls.title: Computer Engineering BSc Imperia – ATHENA assessment

Dates run September 2026–January 2027; the 20 November assessment was moved to 4 December 2026. The 22 January 2027 date is reserved for non-EU students arriving from December onward.

source_urls.evidence: The course uses TE.L.E.MA.CO. for initial preparation assessment. Foreign school-qualification holders follow Italian-language verification and remedial guidance. This course page is not a 2027/28 admission call.

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Modena e Reggio Emilia

source_urls.evidence: BSc Computer Engineering has a separate 2026/27 call, published 11 March 2026. The catalogue classifies the Modena BSc as Italian and restricted access. This BSc is not the existing legacy MSc candidate.

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Padova
universities.research_summary: The 2027/28 international application calls are published; seven program listings on the source page have been verified, while the historic entries remain under review.

source_urls.title: Admission of international students – How to apply
source_urls.evidence: First application call for most programs opens 15 September 2026 and closes 15 November 2026; bachelor's entry normally requires 12 years of schooling; master's applicants need a relevant bachelor’s degree and program-specific requirements; English-taught degrees use apply.unipd.it.

source_urls.title: International students – 2027/28 applications (DiSSGeA)
source_urls.evidence: Lists History (Bachelor’s), Classical Languages and Literatures and Ancient History, Historical Sciences, Landscape Studies, Religious Studies, Local Development and Mobility Studies, and gives calls 15 Sep–15 Nov 2026, 1 Dec 2026–1 Mar 2027, and 1 Apr–1 Jun 2027 for EU and non-EU residents in Italy only.

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Palermo
universities.research_summary: Reviewed the sole legacy MSc candidate individually. Official 2026/27 offer lists Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence (LM-18), with English delivery and historical requirements. Official 2027/28 subject assignments are evidence of teaching only; first-year intake is not confirmed. The international FAQ expressly says exact 2027/28 application dates are unpublished. Fee and scholarship material remains 2026/27; document and deadline discrepancies are recorded. The course regulation is explicitly for 2025/26, although the undated profile repeats its B2 English and curricular routes. Prior-cycle international MSc windows were 15 January–15 March and 15 April–20 July 2026; the first call was free. Foreign-resident non-EU tuition options in 2026/27 were country tariffs of €211/€267/€378 or an income-based route, with €156 fixed tax/stamp charges plus a variable contribution. ERSU benefits depend on income, merit, student classification and available funding. Official second-instalment dates conflict between 29 and 31 December 2026, and the fee-regulation index points to an older PDF than its label states.

source_urls.title: Before Applying – FAQ International Students
source_urls.evidence: Explicitly says exact 2027/28 admission dates have not yet been published; explains that requirements and selection procedures vary by program.

source_urls.title: Degree offer 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: Lists Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, LM-18, Palermo, open access. The university resolution sets a general non-EU-abroad capacity of 30 for conventional open-access courses; the course row does not give a separate quota. This is a 2026/27 offer.

source_urls.title: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence – new-enrolment study plan
source_urls.evidence: The new-enrolment study plan is explicitly labelled 2026/2027, with 2025/2026 in the archive. It does not publish a 2027/28 first-year plan.

source_urls.title: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence – course profile
source_urls.evidence: Names the LM-18 MSc in Palermo and course contact cicsi@unipa.it. Lists B2 English and entry via L-31, L-35, L-8, L-41 or L-30 degrees, another Italian degree with 6 ECTS Mathematics/Physics and 12 ECTS Computing, or an equivalent foreign degree. The profile has no 2027/28 intake declaration.

source_urls.title: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence – course presentation
source_urls.evidence: The course presentation explicitly identifies English as the official teaching language and English thesis writing. This is an undated programme description and cannot establish a new 2027/28 intake.

source_urls.title: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence – teaching regulation, 2025/26
source_urls.evidence: Regulation covers the 2025/26 cohort: LM-18, English, conventional teaching in Palermo. It repeats the course-profile academic routes and B2 English; candidates without L-31 must undergo a Mathematics/Computing interview with the coordinator or teachers. This regulation is not a 2026/27 or 2027/28 call.

source_urls.title: Giovanni Pilato – official teaching assignments
source_urls.evidence: Lists Information Retrieval and Natural Language Processing, 6 ECTS, under Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence in AY 2027/28. It is a teaching assignment and contains no new-entry admission, first-year cohort or application call.

source_urls.title: International Master degrees – 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The international catalogue is labelled enrolling in AY 2026/27 and lists Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence. The page describes two-year second-cycle courses with 120 credits.

source_urls.title: International Students Enrolment
source_urls.evidence: International qualification holders use the dedicated international admission routes. Credential Evaluation Office email is internationalstudents@unipa.it. Visa pre-enrolment does not guarantee a visa.

source_urls.title: Extra-EU international enrolment – 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: For 2026/27 English MSc applications: first call 15 January–15 March; second 15 April–20 July 2026; Universitaly application by 23 August for candidates already applying in UniPa portal; personal-knowledge interviews through 30 November. Requires passport, photo, degree, transcript, language evidence and CV. English route uses UniPa portal assessment followed by Universitaly.

source_urls.title: First international Master call, 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: University notice dated 15 January 2026 gives the first Master application call as 15 January–15 March 2026 and expressly says there is no application fee for that call.

source_urls.title: EU and equivalent foreign-degree enrolment
source_urls.evidence: EU/equivalent applicants use the UniPa Student Portal. After the admission letter, the course coordinator conducts a personal-knowledge interview, including English assessment. Foreign qualifications require original legalised degree and DOV or accepted CIMEA/Diploma Supplement alternatives.

source_urls.title: International language requirements
source_urls.evidence: General guidance lists IELTS Academic 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72, PTE 46, Trinity ISE II–IV and recognised Cambridge/British Institutes qualifications. Its explicit English-certificate exemption is for programmes with a recognised English standardised admission test; it does not repeat the MOI alternative found on the 2026/27 Extra-EU page. No 2027/28 course-specific standard is established.

source_urls.title: International tuition fees – 2026/27 framework
source_urls.evidence: Foreign-resident non-EU students may choose €211/€267/€378 flat charges by country grouping or income assessment through ISEE parificato. The income route has €156 fixed charges (€140 regional tax + €16 stamp) plus a variable contribution. The flat-charge text incorrectly calls all €156 regional tax; the separate contribution table confirms €140 + €16. Financial-document references are for 2024 income and 2026 household/property circumstances.

source_urls.title: Student contribution table, 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The table expressly covers 2026/27 and shows €16 stamp + €140 regional tax. Scientific-area contribution is €370–€2,914 by ISEE before exemptions/reductions. It gives 40%/30%/30% instalments and second-instalment deadline 29 December 2026, whereas the university web fee guide says 31 December.

source_urls.title: Student fees and contributions
source_urls.evidence: Fees comprise stamp, regional tax and income/course-dependent contribution. General schedule is 40% on enrolment, 30% by 31 December 2026 and 30% by 28 February 2027; open-access MSc pays its first instalment when enrolling. The second instalment date conflicts with the 29 December date in the 2026/27 table.

source_urls.title: Student contribution regulation and archive
source_urls.evidence: The latest table is labelled 2026/27. The linked regulation is labelled 2025/26 in force for 2026/27, but its PDF title and text are 2024/25. This document-label discrepancy should be verified before treating its exemption rules as current. No 2027/28 table appears.

source_urls.title: Scholarships for International Students
source_urls.evidence: The page lists ERSU and MAECI as 2026/27 schemes, targeted UNICORE 8.0 for refugee entrants 2026/28, and other older or restricted awards. ERSU is income/merit based and may provide tuition relief, accommodation, meals and cash. No general 2027/28 scholarship call was found.

source_urls.title: ERSU Palermo scholarship and services call, 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: Annual 2026/27 benefit competition: applications 5 June–22 July 2026 at 14:00. Income limits ISEE €23,000 and ISPE €52,500. International applicants need equivalent ISEE and residence documentation, regularisable by 30 November 2026. Monetary amounts depend on ISEE and residence classification; meals/housing values are deducted when provided. For ISEE €11,500–€15,333.33, the off-site gross base is €7,171.11; with both services the cash portion is €4,271.11. Eligibility, merit and available funding apply.

source_urls.title: Student contribution regulation – linked PDF dated 2024/25
source_urls.evidence: The regulation's decree and text expressly state AY 2024/25. The current index labels this link as a 2025/26 regulation in force for 2026/27, creating a document-label mismatch. The PDF alone cannot confirm next-cycle exemptions.

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Parma
universities.research_summary: The official 2027/28 international page says application procedures will be communicated when available. The 2026/27 catalogue lists Data Science for Management as a two-year English LM-Data course with open access subject to requirements verification; its current-cycle intake, admission terms, fees and scholarships remain unverified.

source_urls.title: Admissions for a.y. 2027-2028 – Let’s keep in touch!
source_urls.evidence: Asks international applicants interested in AY 2027/28 to register interest and states that admissions procedures will be communicated once available.

source_urls.title: Data Science for Management – Department of Economics and Management guide 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The Department guide lists Data Science for Management as a second-cycle degree, two years, LM Data Science class, based in Parma, taught entirely in English, open access with verification of requirements and non-mandatory attendance. Its listed first- and second-year plan totals 120 ECTS. These 2026/27 details do not confirm a 2027/28 new-entry intake.

source_urls.title: Data Science for Management – 2025 admission regulations
source_urls.evidence: The 2025-version regulations for LM-DATA require a suitable three-year degree or recognized foreign equivalent, curriculum requirements, individual preparation assessment and English at least B1. Italian graduates with L-18/L-33 or equivalent meet the stated degree-class route; other classes need at least 30 CFU in named economics/business/statistics/mathematics/computing sectors with sub-minima of 9 CFU economics, 6 business, 9 quantitative or computing and 6 statistics. The document lists English evidence routes including IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 60, Cambridge First/Business Vantage, Trinity ISE II or specified TOEIC subscores, and says individual preparation is checked by interview/test. Foreign qualifications are assessed for equivalence. This is a prior-version regulation, not verified 2026/27 or 2027/28 admission guidance.

source_urls.title: Call 26/27 – non-EU future students
source_urls.evidence: For non-EU applicants requiring a study visa, the university says English-taught Master's calls were available and admission opened 15 January 2026. The page directs applicants to degree-specific procedures and does not give Data Science for Management's own deadline or establish 2027/28 dates.

source_urls.title: Tuition and university contributions – 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The 2026/27 fee page lists Data Science for Management and places it in the humanities-social area. The annual charge consists of a €140 regional tax, €16 virtual stamp and a personalized university contribution based on merit, enrollment seniority, disciplinary area and ISEE. The course-specific contribution is not a single fixed amount; this is prior-cycle information and not a 2027/28 quote.

source_urls.title: Fees, scholarships and benefits for international students
source_urls.evidence: The university's international-student fees guidance for the 2026/27 cycle states a €156 first instalment (regional tax and stamp duty) and an approximate €0–€2,000 personalized annual tuition contribution depending on financial circumstances and study area. The amount is not a fixed Data Science for Management quote and is not a 2027/28 estimate.

source_urls.title: ER.GO scholarship and other benefits for international students
source_urls.evidence: The university identifies ER.GO as Emilia-Romagna's higher-education benefits agency. International students may apply for competitive regional scholarships, accommodation and other benefits; applications for the annual call begin when it is published, with household financial documents uploaded through the ER.GO dossier. Amounts, eligibility and deadlines are defined by each call, so no program-specific award or 2027/28 award is implied.

source_urls.title: Study in Parma – LATAM Scholarships 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The 2026/27 call offers five competitive awards of €8,000 gross per year for up to two years plus a tuition exemption to eligible Latin American applicants, but requires B2 Italian and admission to an Italian-taught Master's programme. Data Science for Management is taught in English, so this specific call does not apply to it.

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Pavia
universities.research_summary: The official 2027/28 calendar gives university-wide windows and a €35 fee for non-restricted Master's programs. Computer Engineering is documented in 2026/27 course and admission sources only; its 2027/28 intake and application category remain unconfirmed.

source_urls.title: International Applications – Faculty of Engineering
source_urls.evidence: For foreign applicants to English-taught engineering master's programs, the teaching committee evaluates the academic career and may require a test (usually in September); non-EU applicants need a visa/pre-enrolment, and Computer Engineering applicants must accept an offer. The faculty says it accepts a limited number of non-student applicants per course and gives priority to applicants who accept offers. General faculty guidance; no course-specific 2027/28 call.

source_urls.title: How to apply to Master’s degree programs – 2027/28 calendar
source_urls.evidence: For non-restricted-access Master’s programs, the 2027/28 application windows are 12–18 Nov 2026, 12–20 Jan 2027, 12–22 Mar 2027, 6–12 Jun 2027, and 1–8 Sep 2027. In March and June, non-EU applicants abroad may apply only if spots remain; the September window is for EU and non-EU residents in Italy. The application fee is €35. Restricted-access programs have their own calls and schedules; check the program category and portal listing. These university-wide rules do not confirm Computer Engineering’s 2027/28 intake or category.

source_urls.title: Computer Engineering – official course profile and 2026/27 plan
source_urls.evidence: Lists Computer Engineering as a second-cycle degree, two years, taught entirely in English, LM-32 Computer Systems Engineering, Engineering area, Pavia, and free access. The linked study plan is explicitly for enrollment year 2026/27; this is prior-cycle course evidence and does not establish a 2027/28 first-year intake.

source_urls.title: Computer Engineering course regulations 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The 2026/27 regulations require a recognized qualifying degree, at least 36 basic and 45 specific advanced CFU (81 total across listed subject areas), English at B2, and suitable engineering preparation. The preparation may be assessed in sessions in September–October or January–February; some applicants can be exempt from the assessment based on marks. Foreign qualifications are evaluated case by case. These criteria and dates are prior-cycle regulations, not confirmed 2027/28 conditions.

source_urls.title: Non-EU prospective students – 2026/27 fees
source_urls.evidence: For 2026/27, non-EU students can use a citizenship- and study-area-based flat rate of €390–€4,550 per year without financial documents, or submit financial documents for family-income-based fees. Applicants seeking EDiSU benefits must use the income-based route. The page links the 2026/27 fee table; no 2027/28 amounts are stated.

source_urls.title: Flat-rate tuition brackets 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: For the 2026/27 non-EU flat-rate schedule, the science-area annual amounts are €390, €1,520, or €4,550 for country brackets 1, 2, and 3. Computer Engineering is in the Engineering area. Country bracket and fee-area classification determine the applicable amount; these are not 2027/28 tuition values.

source_urls.title: EDiSU ordinary scholarship call 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The annual 2026/27 call was open to Italian, EU and foreign students, including incoming applicants who intended to apply to Pavia; eligibility depended on income and merit, and funding determined which eligible students became beneficiaries. The 15 September 2026 deadline has passed. Amounts vary by income/geographic status; the official call gives up to €8,248 including a daily meal for eligible off-site students, with different structures for EDiSU college residents. This is regional, not Computer Engineering-specific, and does not establish a 2027/28 award.

source_urls.title: Financial support for international students
source_urls.evidence: The page describes annual EDiSU calls with possible accommodation, one meal per day and an income-based cash amount; it lists the 2026/27 call deadlines and names separate subject scholarships for Civil Engineering for Mitigation of Risk and Environmental Engineering REACH, not Computer Engineering. No dedicated Computer Engineering scholarship is identified on this page; no 2027/28 award is inferred.

source_urls.title: Tuition exemptions and incentives 2026/27
source_urls.source_type: Official fee exemption and incentive guidance
source_urls.evidence: For 2026/27, EDiSU scholarship beneficiaries and eligible non-beneficiaries receive automatic exemption from the all-inclusive tuition fee; equivalent ISEE up to €32,000 also qualifies for full all-inclusive-fee exemption. The page lists a €450 incentive under 2025/26 rules for selected classes including LM-32, but that prior-year award is not a 2026/27 or 2027/28 promise. No 2027/28 rules are stated.

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Perugia
universities.research_summary: The latest official Engineering Management catalogue and course guidance reviewed is for 2026/27. The English BSc and MSc, prior-cycle admission rules, visa route, 2026/27 fees and ADiSU scholarship call are recorded; neither degree's 2027/28 first-year intake or current terms are confirmed.

source_urls.title: Becoming a UniPG student – international admissions
source_urls.evidence: For 2026/27 non-EU applicants residing abroad, the general PICA pre-evaluation window was 29 May–7 June 2026 noon; applicants supplied passport, qualifying-credential documents, language evidence if available and CV, and could apply to only one course. Engineering Management had a dedicated PICA procedure through 21 August 2026; visa applicants to both its BSc and MSc needed an accepted B2 certificate (MOI and other certificates were rejected), and BSc applicants had to provide CEnT-S, TOLC-I or SAT. Positive PICA evaluation was required before Universitaly visa pre-enrolment. The page gives international office contact details. These dates and steps are 2026/27 only and do not establish a 2027/28 call.

source_urls.title: Engineering degree catalogue 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The 2026/27 Department of Engineering catalogue lists Engineering Management as an English-taught three-year L-8 R/L-9 R Bachelor’s and a two-year LM-31 Master’s in Perugia. It also lists other engineering degrees whose teaching is Italian or mixed English/Italian. The catalogue is prior-cycle evidence and does not confirm either course's 2027/28 first-year intake.

source_urls.title: Engineering Management – First cycle degree course
source_urls.evidence: The page, last updated 19 October 2026, describes the three-year English BSc, a sustainable capacity of 180 students, a school-leaving qualification, B2 English, and a mandatory basic-knowledge assessment. It lists TOLC-I, SAT and ACT guidance and OFA rules. The current page does not establish a 2027/28 call or intake.

source_urls.title: Engineering Management – Second cycle degree course
source_urls.evidence: The page, last updated 19 October 2026, describes the English 120-ECTS two-year LM-31 MSc, 80 sustainable places, direct access for L-8/L-9 graduates, an 85-CFU curricular route for other backgrounds, B2 English, committee review of foreign qualifications, and course enrollment guidance. These are current/prior-cycle course details, not a 2027/28 admission call.

source_urls.title: Tuition Fees and scholarships – 2026/27 guidance
source_urls.evidence: The page, last updated 6 October 2026, says exact 2026/27 fees are governed by the University Regulation and gives a usual annual range of €150–€2,200 depending on family income and merit. Applicants whose family income/assets are abroad may use a four-bracket country-based flat contribution or opt for ISEEU Parificato; low-human-development-country and protection-status rules also apply. It does not publish 2027/28 fees.

source_urls.title: ADiSU Umbria scholarship and services call 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The regional 2026/27 call was open to students enrolled or intending to enroll at Umbria institutions, subject to income, enrollment and merit requirements. The published application deadline was 2 September 2026 at noon. ISEE and ISPE limits were €28,339.88 and €61,608.48. Applicants with foreign household income/assets had to submit supporting foreign-income documentation by separate deadlines (2 September or 30 October 2026), following legalization/translation rules. These regional benefits are competitive and are not a program-specific guaranteed award; no 2027/28 call is confirmed.

source_urls.title: ADiSU Umbria 2026/27 scholarship call – official PDF
source_urls.evidence: The 2026/27 call publishes cash amounts by ISEE band and student status plus meal/accommodation values. In the lowest-income band, maximum standard totals include €8,246.78 for an off-site student with paid lodging (cash plus two daily meals), €8,246.78 for an off-site student in an ADiSU bed (cash, bed and meals), €4,819.32 for a commuter (cash plus one daily meal), and €3,623.68 for an in-town student (cash plus one daily meal). Award amounts reduce by income band and depend on eligibility, ranking, service allocation and documentation. Annex 4 lists Engineering Management BSc course L0615 (L-8/L-9) and MSc course M0622 (LM-31) among STEM courses eligible for a 20% cash uplift for women; this uplift is subject to the call's other rules and is not a guaranteed award. This is 2026/27 evidence only.

universities.name: Università di Pisa
universities.research_summary: A department call for three English-taught MSc programs publishes 2027/28 eligibility, dates and a €30 application fee; this does not verify all University of Pisa programs.

source_urls.title: International admissions call 2027/28 – English MSc programs
source_urls.evidence: Department call lists MSc Computer Science, Data Science and Business Informatics, and Informatics for Digital Health. For non-EU applicants residing abroad it gives an application deadline of 1 February 2027 (Anywhere on Earth), notification on 1 March 2027, and a €30 fee per application (up to two). Tuition for 2027/28 is not specified; the call says annual fees are usually announced in June. No seats or acceptance rates are published in this call.

source_urls.title: Master programme in Computer Science
source_urls.evidence: Official page describes the English-taught MSc Computer Science and links to international admissions. Cycle availability is confirmed separately by the 2027/28 department call.

source_urls.title: Master programme in Data Science and Business Informatics
source_urls.evidence: Official page describes the English-taught MSc. Cycle availability is confirmed separately by the 2027/28 department call.

source_urls.title: Master programme in Informatics for Digital Health
source_urls.evidence: Describes an English-taught open-admission MSc and links to foreign-student enrollment for AY 2027/28. The department call confirms cycle availability.

source_urls.title: Degrees offered in English
source_urls.evidence: Department’s English-program directory; the 2027/28 call is the source of cycle-specific availability and dates.

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Salerno
universities.research_summary: Salerno's Computer Science MSc (NF225, LM-18) is a two-year/120-CFU English/Italian degree in the official 2026/27 offer; its Internet of Things curriculum is fully English. International assessment uses Universitaly, document review, a remote programming/database quiz and interview. The 30 September 2026 pre-enrolment deadline is closed; the separate general MSc enrolment deadline is 1 March 2027 and belongs to 2026/27. Tuition depends on ISEE, residence/country and exemptions; a general €15 access-test contribution is not a verified international prescreening fee. The closed UNISA Scholarship 2026/27 offers €1,800 cash plus room/board valued at €6,200, subject to selection and renewal; its mention of 2027/28 is second-year renewal only. ADISURC requires economic, merit and enrolment eligibility. No new 2027/28 course, university application, tuition or scholarship call was identified. The national degree-visa outer application deadline is 31 October 2027, and Salerno may set earlier course deadlines.

source_urls.title: Enrolment – Non-EU citizens abroad
source_urls.evidence: Official non-EU application guidance; the page reviewed does not establish a complete 2027/28 degree-program schedule.

source_urls.title: Enrolment course inventory 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The page explicitly welcomes applicants to 2026/27. Computer Science/Informatica NF225 is an LM-18 Master's with Italian and English teaching; the L-31 Bachelor's is Italian. Course-specific enrolment links control requirements. This does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year offer.

source_urls.title: International teaching: degrees in English 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The explicit 2026/27 inventory lists Computer Science NF225 as English/Italian, rather than identifying every curriculum as English. It lists other BSc, MSc, postgraduate master and PhD categories separately. No new 2027/28 course offer is established.

source_urls.title: Computer Science NF225 course regulation, cohort 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The course's regulation index labels this PDF NF225 cohort 2026/27. It establishes LM-18, two years/120 CFU, five curricula, L-31/L-8 entry or at least 45 CFU in INFO-01/A and IINF-05/A for other classes, individual foreign-curriculum assessment, and readiness assessment. The L-31/L-8 test exemption requires at least 85/110. Its 2026/27 IoT curriculum table marks technical teaching Engl. The English-language examination's B2 learning target is not a universal B2 admission-certificate requirement.

source_urls.title: Computer Science: English Internet of Things curriculum
source_urls.evidence: The course describes five specializations and explicitly says Internet of Things is fully English and lasts two years. This undated presentation is corroborated by the named 2026/27 regulation and is not evidence of a 2027/28 intake.

source_urls.title: Computer Science enrolment: foreign applicants
source_urls.evidence: Applications for 2026/27 are now closed. Relevant Bachelor's preparation and at least 45 computing ECTS are assessed individually. Non-EU applications start on Universitaly; emailed dossiers are not assessed. Positive documentary assessment leads to a compulsory remote C++/Java/database-query quiz and interview. Two interview no-shows cause rejection. Applicants without B2 Italian enter the English IoT curriculum. English evidence may be in CV/academic records; an officially English-taught previous degree avoids further certification under this guidance, while consulates may require a certificate. Contact: international_incoming@cs.unisa.it.

source_urls.title: Computer Science: enrolment and assessment timing
source_urls.evidence: The course page states Master's enrolment 15 July 2026–1 March 2027, ESSE3 registration, assessment in September/February and academic contact gvitiello@unisa.it. One curricular bullet incorrectly names the separate Cloud/Security degree; the NF225 regulation and English Computer Science admission page provide independent course-specific requirements. The general enrolment period is not the earlier non-EU Universitaly deadline.

source_urls.title: Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline: 30 September 2026
source_urls.evidence: The Computer Science department notice published 25 September 2026 states Universitaly pre-enrolment is accepted until 30 September 2026 and later applications will not be assessed. This deadline belongs to the closed 2026/27 intake.

source_urls.title: Non-EU citizens abroad: qualification and visa route
source_urls.evidence: University guidance uses Universitaly for non-EU applicants abroad, university qualification evaluation and subsequent consular visa processing. It mentions November 2026 and also retains an older March 2025 opening reference, so it is not a 2027/28 schedule. Bachelor's qualifications normally follow 12 years of schooling. Italian-taught degree applicants require B2 Italian or the indicated test unless exempt. Recognition documentation may include ENIC-NARIC, an official foreign institution's evidence or a Declaration of Value.

source_urls.title: Tuition and contributions 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The fee page explicitly covers 2026/27 and links the annual fee regulation. The no-tax-area COA exemption has an ISEE ceiling of 30,000 euros and statutory progress/enrolment conditions; payment is through pagoPA in ESSE3. This is not a 2027/28 fee publication.

source_urls.title: Student contribution regulation 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The official PDF was fetched directly with HTTP 200 and parsed after the page's relative link resolved incorrectly in the web tool. Fees comprise income/progress-dependent COA, stamp and regional tax. Regional tax is 130/151/173 euros; foreign-resident households ordinarily use 151 euros. Non-EU non-residents normally use COA band III or band I for listed low-human-development countries, unless eligible ISEE or hardship rules apply. Stamp is 16 euros; foreign-qualification first-year third instalment, if due, is 53 euros. General access-test contribution is 15 euros subject to course exceptions, not a verified IoT prescreening fee. First-year open-access MSc enrolment is due 1 March 2027.

source_urls.title: UNISA Scholarship 2026/27: latest deadline and ranking notice
source_urls.evidence: The university lists 48 scholarships for non-EU international Master's applicants for 2026/27. The latest extended Universitaly submission deadline is 30 June 2026 at 23:59, followed by July rankings. This extension supersedes the original May deadline in the call. The competition is closed.

source_urls.title: UNISA Scholarship call 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The call is for 48 non-EU students resident abroad with suitable foreign degrees. Annual value is 8,000 euros: 1,800 cash after enrolment/payment plus room/board valued at 6,200 for 12 months from 1 October 2026. Required dossier includes CV, B2 language evidence, degree/transcripts, syllabi, two references and the incompatibility declaration. Renewal requires 27 credits by 15 September 2027; its 2027/28 reference is the second year of the 2026/27 intake. It is incompatible with MAECI and duplicate room/board benefits; ADISURC cash-only benefits may be sought under the rules. Tuition and regional payment obligations remain.

source_urls.title: ADISURC scholarship and accommodation competition 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: Published 24 July 2026: the regional competition closed 10 September 2026 at 12:00. Apply through the ADISURC student reserved area; foreign applicants can obtain registration credentials. The notice links the call and CAF/ISEE-equivalent documentation. The competition is not a 2027/28 award.

source_urls.title: ADISURC regional scholarship call 2026/27, English PDF
source_urls.evidence: University of Salerno students are eligible subject to enrolment, merit and financial requirements. ISEE ceiling is 25,500 euros and numeric ISPE ceiling 54,000 euros. Foreign-household ISEEUP must reach ADISURC by 31 March 2027. Base awards at ISEE up to 17,000 euros are 7,171.11 off-site, 4,190.71 commuter and 2,890.16 on-site; service deductions, higher-income reductions and eligible uplifts apply. First years normally need 20 credits by 10 August 2027 for full preservation, or by 30 November for half. Benefits are conditional and do not establish 2027/28 awards.

source_urls.title: Universitaly national international-student procedures 2026/27 and 2027/28
source_urls.evidence: The national page expressly covers 2026/27 and 2027/28. Universitaly is the official free visa-pre-enrolment portal; admission/validation does not guarantee a visa. This does not publish a Salerno course application window or a new first-year offer.

Area D has two awards for two different courses among seven listed English-taught master’s, including Applied Mathematics; the page does not allocate one award specifically to this program. universities.name: Università degli Studi di Torino
universities.research_summary: UniTo's official English-degree catalogue and individual profiles reviewed are for 2026/27. The nine legacy candidates now have current-cycle identities and historical course requirements: five Master's courses are eligible under the prior-cycle Talents4UniTO call, while restricted Business Administration is excluded. The profile for Economics and Finance with Data Science conflicts internally on whether access is locally programmed or open; the 2026/27 Rector's SAT call confirms a quota-based ranking, so the inconsistency remains explicit. The prior-cycle international process used Apply@UniTo, €60 for up to two choices and separate Bachelor's/Master's windows. International tuition used country GDP-PPP bands, with an initial €156 payment and comprehensive contributions from €500 to €1,500; Business and Management and Business Administration had additional €400–€5,100 charges by applicable band. The 2026/27 Talents4UniTO call offered competitive two-year awards of €20,000 total to eligible foreign-degree students in unrestricted English Master's courses; its 2027/28 provision concerns renewal of existing winners only. No 2027/28 first-year offer or current admissions, fees or incoming-student scholarship terms were confirmed for any of the nine candidates. Any 2027/28 year-two coursework displayed on prior-cycle profiles applies to students who entered in 2026/27. Acceptance rates were not officially published in the reviewed sources.

source_urls.title: Application for international students
source_urls.evidence: The reviewed page lists 2026/27 application rounds and a €60 fee; values are retained only as prior-cycle context and are not copied into the active dataset.

Displayed year-two 2027/28 activities belong to the prior cohort.

source_urls.title: International applications for degree-seeking students, AY 2026–2027
source_urls.evidence: The official page explicitly labels the procedure AY 2026–2027. Foreign-qualification applicants used Apply@UniTo, could select up to two programs, and paid €60. It lists prior-cycle postgraduate and undergraduate application windows and distinguishes programs with their own procedures; no 2027/28 dates are provided here.

source_urls.title: Tuition fees for international students
source_urls.evidence: For 2026/27, foreign students residing abroad are charged under country GDP-PPP bands; the first instalment is €156 (€16 stamp duty plus €140 regional tax), with comprehensive contributions of €500, €600, €700, €800, €1,000 or €1,500 by band. Eligibility, ISEE pathways, country categories and possible extra course contributions affect the total; this is historical, not a 2027/28 schedule.

source_urls.title: Courses with additional contributions

source_urls.title: Talents4UniTO call for applications AY 2026–2027
source_urls.evidence: The prior-cycle call offers 40 competitive two-year awards of €20,000 total (€10,000 each year) to eligible non-Italian citizens residing abroad with foreign qualifications entering the first year of eligible unrestricted English-taught Master's programs. It lists AI/HPC, Economics, Language Technologies and Digital Humanities, Molecular Biotechnology, and Stochastics and Data Science among eligible programs; Business Administration is excluded as restricted-access. Its AY 2027/28 clause covers renewal by existing 2026/27 awardees entering year two, not new first-year awards.

source_urls.title: Admission call for selected Bachelor's degrees using SAT, AY 2026–2027
source_urls.evidence: The 2026/27 call confirms a SAT-based preregistration and ranking with finite quotas. Business and Management quotas are 200 domestic/EU/equivalent residents, 40 non-EU visa applicants and 10 Marco Polo places; Economics and Finance with Data Science quotas are 195, 50 and 5. Procedure 1 preregistration was 1–19 June 2026 with SAT valid by 6 June; procedure 2 was 1 July–14 September 2026 with SAT valid by 12 September. Economics and Finance with Data Science used a Math score threshold in the first procedure. Historical figures only.

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Trento
universities.research_summary: UniTrento's seven remaining legacy course rows now have official 2026/27 profile and call evidence: Computer Science (LM-18), Artificial Intelligence Systems (LM-32), Data Science (LM-DATA), Human-Computer Interaction (LM-55 R), Cognitive Science (LM-55), International Security Studies (LM-52 R joint with Sant’Anna), and the English-taught CEILS Bachelor's (L-14 R). The records include their prior-cycle durations, language, locations, entry requirements, reserved places, application routes and fees. The CEILS row now uses the complete official title; International Security Studies (MISS) remains separate from the Erasmus Mundus Security, Intelligence and Strategic Studies (IMSISS). 2026/27 non-EU fee and scholarship rules varied by programme and score, so they are stored only as historical. The previously confirmed seven 28DIGITAL tracks remain distinct and unchanged. No 2027/28 first-year offer or named admission call, fees, or new-entry awards were confirmed for these seven legacy programmes, and their active availability status remains pending. Official applicant totals were not published in the reviewed sources, so no course acceptance rate is inferred.

source_urls.title: 28DIGITAL Master School at UniTrento – technical majors and 2027/28 intake
source_urls.source_type: Official department and program admissions page
source_urls.evidence: Describes the UniTrento 28DIGITAL offer as two-year, 120-ECTS double-degree master’s study with technical majors in Information Engineering (Cloud and Network Infrastructures and HPC; Intelligent Chips and Systems), Computer Science (Cyber Security, Data Science, Fintech, Human-Computer Interaction & Design with extended reality), and Artificial Intelligence Systems (Artificial Intelligence with Affective Computing). For the 2027/28 intake it lists three application periods: 31 Oct–11 Feb open to EU/EEA/CH and non-EU applicants; 11 Feb–15 Apr open to EU/EEA/CH and non-EU Italian residents, with visa timing limitations; and 15 Apr–1 Jun open to EU/EEA/CH and non-EU Italian residents. The page says not all trajectories may be available in period two, central selection is handled by 28DIGITAL, and consortium scholarships are first-come-first-served. UniTrento's additional double-degree scholarships are for second-year entrants who receive no other 28DIGITAL grant; their call is indicatively published in August.

source_urls.title: 28DIGITAL Master School – 2027 admission dates and criteria
source_urls.evidence: Lists 2027 application periods as 30 Oct 2026–31 Jan 2027, 1 Feb–18 Apr 2027 and 19 Apr–31 May 2027, with applicant-category/visa restrictions by round. States all 28DIGITAL programmes are taught in English; applicants need a relevant bachelor’s degree of at least 180 ECTS and English proficiency, generally IELTS 6.5 with section minimums or TOEFL iBT scores depending on test scale/date. The University of Trento department’s 2027/28 intake page publishes different round boundaries; treat the university-level date comparison as conflicting and use each programme’s central portal before applying.

source_urls.evidence: Lists €75 non-refundable application fee per application, €250 non-refundable registration deposit credited to first-semester tuition, and tuition of €6,000 per academic year for EU/EEA citizens or €18,000 for non-EU/EEA citizens. General merit-based awards include full or half tuition waivers; additional excellence scholarships with living allowance are restricted to EU/EEA and associated-country citizens in selected programs. Period 1, 2 and 3 tuition-payment expected deadlines are 31 May, 30 June and 19 July 2027, respectively.

source_urls.title: DISI Master's admission call for non-European citizens abroad, AY 2026–2027

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Trieste
universities.research_summary: Trieste's former Data Science and Scientific Computing MSc was dismissed in 2023 and replaced by Data Science and Artificial Intelligence and Scientific and Data-Intensive Computing; the latter explicitly allows no first-year admission. The former candidate remains visible and DSAI is a separate English-taught, blended two-year MSc supported by 2026/27 evidence. Physics is a two-year MSc taught in English and Italian. Both current candidates require degree/curricular and personal-preparation assessment; the 2026/27 foreign-qualification route used ApplyNow, EUR40 for up to three programmes, then course checks/ESSE3 and Universitaly for visa applicants. The 2026/27 abroad-resident standard is EUR800 tuition plus EUR160 regional tax and EUR16 stamp, conditional on progress/duration eligibility; ARDiS awards have separate economic, merit and housing rules. The course pages' 31 March 2027 enrolment end differs from the catalogue's 30 March statement. No 2027/28 first-year offer, course-specific dates/quotas, fee schedule or scholarship call was identified. The national 31 October 2027 visa-application ceiling does not establish a university application deadline.

source_urls.title: Application

source_urls.title: Degree seekers: 2026/27 assessment rounds and application fee
source_urls.evidence: Last updated 2 October 2026. Foreign-qualification assessment for 2026/27 used apply.units.it: 15 December 2025–15 January 2026; 15 February–30 April 2026; EU/equivalent-only round until 2 October 2026. Fee EUR40 for up to three programmes. No 2027/28 university assessment calendar or fee was identified.

source_urls.title: UniTS pre-enrolment for visa applicants
source_urls.evidence: Non-EU residents abroad needing a visa must check available quotas, obtain positive assessment on ApplyNow, pre-enrol through Universitaly, complete the course's enrolment/payment requirements and upload the residence-permit application receipt after arrival. Contact international.students@amm.units.it. Admission does not guarantee a visa. Undated annual process guidance is not a 2027/28 course offer.

source_urls.title: International students: required documents
source_urls.evidence: Updated 24 July 2025. Bachelor entry normally requires a qualifying diploma after at least 12 school years. MSc entry requires Bachelor/equivalent, transcript or EU Diploma Supplement, and official course descriptions. Translate non-Italian/non-English documents; legalization/apostille rules have stated country exceptions. UniTS says a DOV is not needed; CIMEA comparability may be requested in special cases. Follow individual assessment instructions for originals and language proof.

source_urls.title: UniTS published visa quota table: updated 16 January 2026
source_urls.evidence: The quota table, last updated 16 January 2026, lists DSAI MSc 25 places and Physics MSc 10 including 2 Marco Polo places. The visible table does not state an academic year. Record only dated published-table context; do not relabel these figures as 2027/28 quotas or derive an acceptance rate.

source_urls.title: Ministerial international-student procedures 2026/27 and 2027/28
source_urls.source_type: Official ministerial procedure PDF hosted by university
source_urls.evidence: Ministerial memorandum valid for both 2026/27 and 2027/28: visa pre-enrolment uses Universitaly; the national last date to lodge a 2027/28 degree-study visa application is 31 October 2027, while universities may set earlier dates. A type-D entrant must apply for a residence permit within eight working days. This is a national framework, not a UniTS course application window or intake confirmation; Italian original prevails.

source_urls.title: University fees 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The university page's 2026/27 framework has income/residence-dependent tuition, stamp duty and regional tax. Italy residents use timely ISEE Universita; residents abroad use flat reduced fees. MSc first-window instalments: 19 December 2026, 31 March and 28 May 2027; second-window: 31 March, 28 May and 15 June 2027, subject to course-specific first-enrolment deadlines. Payment is through PagoPA/ESSE3. ARDiS exemptions are applied after official eligibility lists. Fee-office contact tasse.studenti@amm.units.it.

source_urls.title: Fee notice 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The 2026/27 notice sets first-year initial instalment EUR250 (16 stamp, 120 initial regional tax, 114 tuition). Abroad residents meeting progress/duration requirements pay EUR800 tuition plus EUR160 regional tax and EUR16 stamp; failure adds 20% to tuition (EUR960). Italy-resident qualifying ISEE up to EUR30,000 gives zero tuition; above EUR75,000/no ISEE tuition is EUR2,900, or EUR3,195 without progress/duration eligibility. Timely ISEE is required. These are annual conditional rates, not 2027/28 fees.

source_urls.title: ARDiS regional university benefits 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: 2026/27 regional benefit applications opened 15 July 2026 at 10:00; deadlines are 13:00 Italy time by benefit. University enrolment, merit and economic requirements apply together; ISEE ceiling EUR28,339.88 and ISPE ceiling EUR61,608.48. Foreign-household cases need ISEE parificato through affiliated CAF. Trieste contact info.trieste@ardis.fvg.it. No 2027/28 competition is established.

source_urls.title: ARDiS unified call updated 14 October 2026
source_urls.evidence: 2026/27 scholarship deadline 17 September 2026 at 13:00 CEST; first-year housing deadline 27 August. Standard gross scholarship amounts: off-site EUR7,171.11, commuter EUR4,190.71, on-site EUR2,890.16; income thresholds reduce or increase amounts, with separate STEM-women provisions. Housing charges are deducted from scholarship for assigned accommodation, so gross figures are not all cash. First-years need the call's 20-CFU merit condition to retain full benefits. Foreign-income documentation and incompatible-award rules apply.

source_urls.title: Bachelor's and master's enrolment: ESSE3
source_urls.evidence: UniTS directs applicants to degree-specific requirements and says foreign qualifications/visa applicants must first follow international procedures. ESSE3 is used for test/preparation registrations, enrolment applications and fee payments. ApplyNow is the separate foreign-qualification assessment portal.

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Udine
universities.research_summary: Udine's official 2026/27 Computer Science profile identifies an unrestricted-access two-year, 120-credit LM-18 MSc in Udine taught in Italian; the old English-language tracker label was incorrect. Applicants needed an L-31/L-8 (or former 26/9) degree or at least 24 relevant computing and mathematics credits. The course committee reviews preparation and English at approximately B2 and can require a test or interview; the course page exempts graduates with at least 90/110. Non-EU residents and/or foreign-degree holders followed the 2026/27 Elix-Forms assessment process (1 February–31 May, €20), then Universitaly, with 30 June 2026 as the prior-cycle visa pre-enrolment deadline. This differs from the course's separate 5 October 2026 enrolment deadline and justified-motives extension to 30 April 2027. The 2026/27 additional tuition notice lists contribution and fixed-charge components; the international student page reports a different total fee ceiling. The discrepancy is preserved. ARDiS scholarships and housing were competitive 2026/27 regional benefits. No 2027/28 Computer Science first-year offer, application call, fee schedule or scholarship call was identified.

source_urls.title: How to apply
source_urls.evidence: States that annual rules, deadlines and tests are listed in the prospectus published each June; non-EU applicants follow pre-enrolment and course-level reserved-place procedures.

source_urls.title: Computer Science MSc course profile
source_urls.evidence: Official profile identifies Computer Science as an unrestricted-access, two-year 120-credit LM-18 Master's degree in Udine. The language of instruction is Italian. This is course identity and 2026/27 context, not confirmation of a 2027/28 first-year intake.

source_urls.title: Computer Science course admission requirements
source_urls.evidence: Applicants need a suitable three-year degree. Curricular eligibility is an L-31 or L-8 degree (or former classes 26 or 9), or at least 24 CFU in relevant computer-science and mathematics subjects. A committee checks preparation and English at approximately B2; an interview or test may be required, except the page exempts graduates with at least 90/110. Listed 2026 dates are 9 July–5 October, with a justified-motives extension to 30 April 2027.

source_urls.title: Mathematics, Computer Science and Physics study prospectus 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The official faculty prospectus lists Informatica LM-18 among active Master's courses and explicitly says it is taught in Italian. It gives course-specific admission rules and dates; its 2027/28 offering is not established.

source_urls.title: Additional Notice for applicants with foreign qualifications 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: For second-cycle courses taught in Italian or English, non-EU residents and/or holders of foreign qualifications used Elix-Forms pre-evaluation from 1 February to 31 May 2026, with a non-refundable €20 fee and academic review within 30 working days. Successful applicants then used Universitaly; the 2026/27 pre-enrolment deadline was 30 June 2026. Applicants to Italian-taught courses needed Italian B2. These are closed prior-cycle terms only.

source_urls.title: Admission requirements for applicants with foreign qualifications
source_urls.evidence: The University directs foreign-degree Master's applicants to the Additional Notice for the relevant academic year, its annual prospectus and the course's own requirements. The page specifies the Additional Notice available at review as 2026/27 and gives the Elix-Forms assessment dates for that cycle; it does not publish 2027/28 course deadlines.

source_urls.title: Additional Notice on tuition, contributions and exemptions 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The 2026/27 notice sets the annual university contribution from €0 to €2,000, stamp duty €16 and regional tax €120–€160, subject to conditions and exemptions; payment is normally in three instalments. It is a prior-cycle framework, not a 2027/28 quote.

source_urls.title: Useful information for international students: fees and benefits
source_urls.evidence: The international-student page reports 2026/27 fees between €16 and €2,076 and three instalments. The University's separate tuition page reports €16–€2,026, and its 2026/27 Additional Notice gives conditional components rather than that same range. The published totals differ; retain the discrepancy and do not choose a single total.

source_urls.title: ARDiS Unified Call for regional student benefits 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: The call covers eligible students at Udine and Trieste. It requires enrollment plus economic and merit eligibility; foreign households use ISEE parificato. The 2026/27 ISEE and ISPE ceilings were €28,339.88 and €61,608.48. Awards and housing are competitive annual benefits, not guaranteed course-specific grants.

source_urls.title: ARDiS 2026/27 application opening and deadlines
source_urls.evidence: Online regional-benefit applications opened 15 July 2026. The scholarship deadline was 17 September at 13:00; new-student housing applications closed 27 August at 13:00. These are closed prior-cycle dates only.

universities.name: Università degli Studi di Verona
universities.research_summary: The Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine MSc is listed in 2026/27 sources, and its 2026/27 admission routes, eligibility and scholarship call are documented as prior-cycle evidence. Its study plan activates year two in 2027/28 for the 2026/27 cohort; a new 2027/28 first-year intake and terms remain unverified.

source_urls.title: International degree-seeking students
source_urls.evidence: Reviewed page states 2026/27 international master's call status; it does not confirm 2027/28 program availability or deadlines.

source_urls.title: Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine – course profile
source_urls.evidence: The profile identifies a two-year Master's degree, class LM-6 R, taught in English in Verona, with limited entry by qualifications. The displayed profile is for 2026/27 and does not establish a 2027/28 first-year intake.

source_urls.title: Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine – 2026/27 admissions
source_urls.evidence: For 2026/27, the course page lists 35 total places, 5 reserved for specified non-EU applicants, qualification-based selection, applications 1 July–31 August 2026 by 10:00 Italian time, first ranking on 18 September 2026 and a €50 admission fee. These are prior-cycle values.

source_urls.title: Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine – admission requirements
source_urls.evidence: The reviewed page is for 2026/27. It describes qualifying biology/biotechnology and other degree classes or specified science credits, an English B2 requirement with listed exemptions, and a separate set of criteria for applicants with degrees earned abroad; it does not confirm 2027/28 requirements.

source_urls.title: International admission call – Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine, 2026/27
source_urls.evidence: Separate 2026/27 call for applicants with a foreign degree, non-Italian citizenship and no residence in Italy: 5 reserved places; relevant first-level degree; weighted CGPA above 81%; English B2 or a prior English-taught qualification; application 2 February–31 March 2026 at 15:00 Italian time; €50 pre-admission fee. It also lists one €8,000 gross/year scholarship with tuition exemption and four €1,000 flat-rate contributions for two academic years. This is historical evidence and must not be added to or assumed for 2027/28.

source_urls.title: Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine – 2026/27 cohort study plan
source_urls.evidence: The study plan for students enrolled in 2026/27 says the second year will activate in 2027/28. This confirms planned second-year teaching for that cohort only and is not a new-entry admission notice.

official_program_source_urls.title: Admission to two-year Master's degrees 2026/27
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The mandatory prior-to-enrolment Esse3 process accepted one MSc preference per candidate after the bachelor's degree. 2026/27 application windows ran 28 July–15 September, then monthly windows through 10 May 2027. Eligibility checks covered the degree, curricular CFU, individual preparation and required English level. Eligible applicants enrolled 22 September 2026–20 May 2027; admission and enrollment are separate stages.

official_program_source_urls.title: Computer Engineering teaching regulations 2026/27
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Regulation identifies Class LM-32, 120 ECTS, two-year standard duration, English instruction, and three curricula. Admission requires a suitable bachelor's degree, at least 48 ECTS in listed engineering, computing, mathematics, physics and related areas, adequate preparation and English B2. Admission may require curricular integrations completed before entry; no educational debt is permitted.

official_program_source_urls.title: General overview for international candidates 2026/27
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Foreign-qualification evaluation requires academic records and proof of qualification authenticity. Visa applicants also submit Universitaly pre-enrolment; the 2026/27 page states a national visa-application outer date of 30 November 2026. Computer Engineering is an English-taught MSc, so foreign candidates use the Master's Esse3 assessment route and English evidence; Italian B2 applies to programmes taught in Italian. These are 2026/27 procedures only.

official_program_source_urls.title: Admissions to first-level degree courses
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The official page says 2027/28 admission call instructions for first-level degrees will be published in February 2027.

official_program_source_urls.title: English B2 assessment for Master's degrees 2026/27
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Computer Engineering is included in the 2026/27 Master's language-assessment list. The online English test has 30 questions, lasts 15 minutes and requires at least 21/30; applicants may register up to three working days before published test sessions. This calendar is prior-cycle only.

official_program_source_urls.title: Computer Engineering MSc profile
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The official profile lists the two-year English-taught Computer Engineering Master's at Bari. Current curricula are Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, Cybersecurity and Cloud, and Cyberphysical Systems. This is prior-cycle profile evidence only.

official_program_source_urls.title: ADISU Puglia benefits and scholarship call 2026/27
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The regional annual benefits call covered eligible students at the Polytechnic University of Bari. Degree-course applications ran 14 July–13 August 2026, noon, online. Awards and services are competitive and subject to the call's economic, merit, enrollment and documentation criteria; no Computer Engineering award is guaranteed.

official_program_source_urls.title: Student fees and contributions regulations 2026/27
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The annual all-inclusive contribution is income- and eligibility-dependent; it is zero in the no-tax area at ISEE ≤€26,000 when applicable criteria are satisfied and is capped at €2,257.60 for ISEE ≥€90,000 or absent eligible ISEE, before any late-payment or study-progress penalties. ADISU regional tax and €16 stamp duty are separate; normal contributions are divided across four payments. Merit and aid exemptions have additional conditions.

official_program_source_urls.title: Tuition and fee information 2026/27
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The 2026/27 calculator is ISEE-based and does not include merit reductions, exemptions or penalties. The initial enrollment installment is €136 (€120 regional tax plus €16 stamp duty); the regional contribution is adjusted at T2 according to the eligible ISEE. The annual all-inclusive contribution depends on the fee regulation and student circumstances.

official_program_source_urls.title: Targeted scholarship for Palestinian students from Gaza 2026/27
official_program_source_urls.source_type: Official targeted international scholarship call PDF
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The call offered one €22,000 gross award across two years to a Palestinian student resident in Gaza already admitted to a 2026/27 Poliba MSc. It includes €11,000 gross per year, full fee exemption and arrival/psychological support. Deadline was 23 October 2026. Second-year payment requires at least 12 CFU by 31 July 2027 and enrollment in 2027/28; the scholarship is incompatible with ADISU aid and is not a general 2027/28 new-entry award.

official_program_source_urls.title: PoliBa scholarships and international-student support
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The official index lists 2026/27 merit, international-student and other calls. Merit lists shown are for enrolled students and the previous cycle; do not treat them as first-year guarantees. It also records a 2026/27 one-scholarship call for Palestinian students resident in Gaza, restricted to candidates already admitted to an MSc and not compatible with ADISU aid.

official_program_source_urls.title: Computer Science and Engineering MSc profile
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Identifies a two-year English-taught Master of Science at Milano Leonardo. The course is 120 ECTS and offers Computer Science and Engineering, Business and Innovation, and Artificial Intelligence study plans. Foreign-degree applicants need a comparable first-cycle qualification and their academic background is assessed against programme criteria; the profile is not a 2027/28 first-year offer.

official_program_source_urls.title: Master of Science programme catalogue
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The official catalogue lists 45 Laurea Magistrale programmes, including Computer Science and Engineering, Cyber Risk Strategy and Governance, High Performance Computing Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Space Engineering, Design & Engineering, Architecture, Communication Design and Civil Engineering. It lists no standalone MSc named Artificial Intelligence or Aerospace Engineering. The list is current catalogue evidence, not a named 2027/28 first-year intake notice.

official_program_source_urls.title: Deadlines – Admission to Laurea Magistrale with foreign qualification
official_program_source_urls.evidence: For September 2027 MSc entry, the page gives general 2027/28 windows of 1 Oct–1 Dec 2026 (early bird), 12–28 Jan 2027 and 1–18 Mar 2027 for EEA and certain non-EEA residents in Italy. Architecture/Design has its own table with a 1 Oct 2026–28 Jan 2027 general call and the same additional March call. A separate Engineering subsection labelled 2026/27 nevertheless describes the September 2027 intake and gives 12 Jan–25 Feb 2027, creating a cycle/date discrepancy that must be resolved by study area. Fees are €50 early bird or €150 standard, and candidates may apply to at most two programmes.

official_program_source_urls.title: Documents required by the Admissions Office – English certification
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Gives 2027/28 English certificate scores for MSc applicants: TOEFL iBT at least 78 for tests through 20 Jan 2026 and at least 4.5 from 21 Jan 2026; TOEIC at least 785 Listening/Reading and 310 Speaking/Writing; IELTS at least 6; specified Cambridge, Trinity, Pearson and LanguageCert scores. Applicants whose bachelor’s was taught in English for at least three years may be exempt if their university certifies at least 75% of courses were in English.

official_program_source_urls.title: Merit Based Call for Applications – A.Y. 2027–2028
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Offers 10 Platinum (€10,000 gross), 18 Gold (€8,000 gross), 16 Piacenza Gold (€5,000 gross), 10 Piacenza Bronze (€2,500 gross), and 10 Silver awards (tuition waiver at Cremona, Lecco, Mantova and Piacenza); all include a tuition waiver for the award year. Eligible applicants must be international first-year MSc applicants to English-taught programs for 2027/28 and must have paid the admission application fee during 1 Oct–1 Dec 2026. Scholarship forms are accepted 1 Oct–15 Dec 2026 at noon Italian time. Awards are competitive and subject to admission and acceptance conditions.

official_program_source_urls.title: Cyber Risk Strategy and Governance MSc profile
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The official page expressly says its information is for 2025/26 and may change in 2026/27. It identifies a two-year English MSc at the Milan partner-university campus, delivered with Bocconi. Foreign-degree applicants are evaluated competitively by a joint committee using transcript, curriculum and motivation letter; the page says there are no fixed admission criteria. This historical profile does not prove 2026/27 or 2027/28 intake.

official_program_source_urls.title: Master of Science programme catalogue
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The official catalogue lists 45 Laurea Magistrale programmes, including Computer Science and Engineering, Cyber Risk Strategy and Governance, High Performance Computing Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Space Engineering, Design & Engineering, Architecture, Communication Design and Civil Engineering. It lists no standalone MSc named Artificial Intelligence or Aerospace Engineering. The list is current catalogue evidence, not a named 2027/28 first-year intake notice.

official_program_source_urls.title: Deadlines – Admission to Laurea Magistrale with foreign qualification
official_program_source_urls.evidence: For September 2027 MSc entry, the page gives general 2027/28 windows of 1 Oct–1 Dec 2026 (early bird), 12–28 Jan 2027 and 1–18 Mar 2027 for EEA and certain non-EEA residents in Italy. Architecture/Design has its own table with a 1 Oct 2026–28 Jan 2027 general call and the same additional March call. A separate Engineering subsection labelled 2026/27 nevertheless describes the September 2027 intake and gives 12 Jan–25 Feb 2027, creating a cycle/date discrepancy that must be resolved by study area. Fees are €50 early bird or €150 standard, and candidates may apply to at most two programmes.

official_program_source_urls.title: Documents required by the Admissions Office – English certification
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Gives 2027/28 English certificate scores for MSc applicants: TOEFL iBT at least 78 for tests through 20 Jan 2026 and at least 4.5 from 21 Jan 2026; TOEIC at least 785 Listening/Reading and 310 Speaking/Writing; IELTS at least 6; specified Cambridge, Trinity, Pearson and LanguageCert scores. Applicants whose bachelor’s was taught in English for at least three years may be exempt if their university certifies at least 75% of courses were in English.

official_program_source_urls.title: Merit Based Call for Applications – A.Y. 2027–2028
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Offers 10 Platinum (€10,000 gross), 18 Gold (€8,000 gross), 16 Piacenza Gold (€5,000 gross), 10 Piacenza Bronze (€2,500 gross), and 10 Silver awards (tuition waiver at Cremona, Lecco, Mantova and Piacenza); all include a tuition waiver for the award year. Eligible applicants must be international first-year MSc applicants to English-taught programs for 2027/28 and must have paid the admission application fee during 1 Oct–1 Dec 2026. Scholarship forms are accepted 1 Oct–15 Dec 2026 at noon Italian time. Awards are competitive and subject to admission and acceptance conditions.

programs.program: Hydrogen Systems and Enabling Technologies (HySET Erasmus Mundus Joint Master)

official_program_source_urls.title: HySET admission requirements
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Requires a relevant bachelor’s degree of at least 180 ECTS in listed engineering/science fields; minimum English evidence is TOEFL iBT 90 with at least 21 in each section, IELTS 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 each section, or Cambridge 160 (higher threshold for a TU/e destination). Selection is scored on academic achievements, background relevance, references/video, and experience. The current page states a 2027–29 call is open.

official_program_source_urls.title: HySET applications open for the 2027–2029 edition
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Official announcement says the fifth HySET edition covers academic years 2027–2029 and opened 1 October 2026; the application deadline is 15 November 2026. HySET is jointly coordinated by Politecnico di Torino and Politecnico di Milano with international consortium partners.

official_program_source_urls.title: HySET continuation beyond 2026 – funding and admissions
official_program_source_urls.evidence: States that funding for the 2027 cohort had not yet been secured and future scholarships depend on a successful external funding award; scholarship availability is not guaranteed. The separate self-funded page states annual fees of €4,500 for European students and €9,000 for non-European students.

official_program_source_urls.title: HySET programme structure and awarded degrees
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Describes a 120-ECTS four-semester master’s, with first-year entry allocated between Politecnico di Torino and Politecnico di Milano and second-year mobility to a consortium partner. Depending on the partner route, students earn two master’s degrees; the programme focuses on the hydrogen value chain.

official_program_source_urls.title: HySET frequently asked questions – language of instruction
official_program_source_urls.evidence: States that the entire HySET programme is taught in English.

official_program_source_urls.title: HySET self-funded students – tuition fees

official_program_source_urls.title: Digital Skills for Sustainable Societal Transitions MSc profile

official_program_source_urls.title: 2026/27 entry requirements for Master's programmes
official_program_source_urls.evidence: The official one-page annex gives course-specific language minima and recommended academic backgrounds. official_program_source_urls.title: Admissions and enrolment – Master's degree programmes
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Polito states that its master's programmes last two full-time academic years and total 120 ECTS. The listed special selection calls are for 2026/27; the reviewed page does not name the general 2027/28 candidate-course calls.

official_program_source_urls.title: Applicants with a non-Italian qualification – Master's degree programmes
official_program_source_urls.evidence: For the 2026/27 cycle, applicants need a foreign first-cycle degree giving access to second-cycle study, suitable academic performance, programme-specific curricular requirements and language evidence. English-taught programmes require English B2; Italian or mixed Italian/English programmes require English B2 and Italian B2. Applicants can select up to two programmes. The page gives 2026/27 calls (including a third call restricted to EU and non-EU residents in Italy) and a €50 application fee; these are historical and do not set 2027/28 dates or fees.

official_program_source_urls.evidence: Profile identifies a separate English-taught, two-year/120-CFU, open-access LM-21 degree in Rome. official_program_source_urls.title: Sustainable Coastal and Ocean Engineering LM-23
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Profile identifies a separate English-taught, two-year/120-CFU, open-access LM-23 degree at Ostia, with 16 November 2026 enrollment deadline. This is one possible Engineering degree, not an established match to legacy-096.

official_program_source_urls.title: Bando Lauree Magistrali 2026/27 – Engineering sections
official_program_source_urls.evidence: Engineering sections require a suitable first-cycle/equivalent degree, course-regulation curricular requirements and prior-career assessment. B2 English is stated for Sustainable Coastal/Ocean, Aerospace and Biomedical. The annual call distinguishes a 70-euro Italian language test and a 60-euro supplementary assessment surcharge; neither establishes a generic 2027/28 application fee.

official_program_source_urls.title: Offerta formativa in lingua inglese e doppi titoli
