sources.evidence: Says all international students, EU and non-EU, are invited to pre-admission for curriculum evaluation; a positive result is followed by Universitaly pre-enrolment where relevant. Gives the Welcome Office contact and describes visa handling and annual ERDIS aid in general terms. Any timing on the page is not a 2027/28 deadline.

sources.title: Application
sources.evidence: General international application instructions; no program-specific 2027/28 deadline was confirmed in the material reviewed.

sources.title: International students
sources.evidence: Official general international admissions guidance and route to annual calls; it does not establish a 2027/28 Computer Science call or deadline.

sources.title: Enrolment – Non-EU citizens abroad
sources.evidence: Official non-EU application guidance; the page reviewed does not establish a complete 2027/28 degree-program schedule.

sources.title: International Students Office
sources.evidence: The cycle-specific information reviewed is for 2026/27; the 2027/28 program calls remain outstanding.

sources.title: International Students
sources.evidence: University page directs international students to degree-specific procedures and notes that rules and deadlines vary by program; no 2027/28 program facts are confirmed here.

sources.title: Enrolment
sources.evidence: The University describes its 2026/27 admissions processes and says calls contain the applicable admission requirements, tests, places, rankings and enrollment procedures. It does not confirm any 2027/28 course call.

sources.title: Master's Degree Programmes – 2026/27 catalogue
sources.evidence: The official 2026/27 catalogue lists Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence for Science and Technology, Data Science for Economics and Health, and Bioinformatics for Computational Genomics. The individual pages establish distinct language and admissions classifications; this catalogue is not a 2027/28 intake notice.

sources.title: Computer Science – Master's degree profile
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 course is an LM-18, two-year, 120-ECTS open-access Master's in Milan taught in Italian and English. L-31 graduates may apply; other degrees need at least 48 credits in INF/01 or ING-INF/05 and 12 credits in MAT/01–09; foreign qualifications are assessed for equivalence and preparation, with an interview possible. The study plan includes a 3-ECTS B2 English proficiency activity.

sources.title: Computer Science – admission notice AY 2026/27
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 notice gives open-admission applications 22 January–30 October 2026, non-EU visa-applicant deadline 30 April, €30 application fee, enrolment 5 May 2026–15 January 2027, and apply.unimi.it for foreign qualifications. The listed deadlines and fee are prior-cycle only.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence for Science and Technology – inter-university profile
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 profile identifies the English-taught, two-year, 120-ECTS LM-91 joint degree run by Milano-Bicocca, the University of Milan, and Pavia. Bicocca is the administrative headquarters and handles admissions. Requirements include a Bachelor's degree, at least 30 CFU across listed computer science, engineering, mathematics, statistics or physics sectors, and English at B2 or higher.

sources.title: Data Science for Economics and Health – Master's profile
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 profile identifies a two-year, 120-ECTS, English-taught LM-Data Master's in Milan, open access with entry-requirements examination. It links the annual admission procedure; it does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

sources.title: Data Science for Economics and Health – admission notice AY 2026/27
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 notice requires a Bachelor's degree and at least 30 ECTS across computer science/mathematics, economics/statistics, and/or medical sciences, B2 English, and a written online assessment with possible interview. Applications ran 22 January–20 July 2026 (visa applicants by 30 April), cost €30, and used apply.unimi.it for foreign qualifications. These are prior-cycle conditions and dates.

sources.title: Bioinformatics for Computational Genomics – Master's profile
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 course is a two-year, 120-ECTS, English-taught LM-8 R joint degree organized by the University of Milan and Politecnico di Milano, with first-year enrollment open, limited enrollment and an admission test. The profile lists 50 places plus 10 reserved for non-EU candidates applying for a visa.

sources.title: Bioinformatics for Computational Genomics – admission call AY 2026/27
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 call accepts Biology/Life Science degrees with at least 30 CFU in biological areas and 18 CFU in genetics, molecular biology and biochemistry, or CS/engineering/physics/math/statistics degrees with at least 30 CFU in relevant quantitative areas including 6 CFU mathematics and 12 CFU in specified computing/statistics sectors. English B2 is required; interview/scoring rules differ by applicant group. Applications ran 24 March–26 June for most applicants and to 29 May for non-EU visa applicants; €30 fee; 50 places plus 10 visa-reserved. No 2027/28 call is established.

sources.title: International enrolment in degree programmes
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, non-EU applicants residing abroad needed a Universitaly pre-enrolment by 31 July; master's applicants with foreign qualifications completed documentation through apply.unimi.it, including translated/legalized degrees and CIMEA/DOV or accepted equivalents. This general guidance is prior-cycle only.

sources.title: Fees – current year AY 2026/27
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, the first instalment is a fixed €156. Tuition for students with income abroad varies by country group and course tuition area: Group A €200/€256, Group B €910/€1,164, Group C €3,204/€4,101.12 for Areas A/B; regional tax may remain due for Groups B/C. Students with eligible ISEE have a no-tax area up to €30,000 subject to merit. Amounts are prior-cycle and exact area/country eligibility must be checked.

sources.title: University scholarships AY 2026/27
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, the University offered 1,055 awards of €1,800 for students above the income threshold for regional DSU scholarships; applications ran 10 July–30 September 2026. Eligibility and merit rules are in the annual call. This is not a guaranteed award for any program or a 2027/28 offer.

sources.title: European Futures Scholarships AY 2026/27
sources.source_type: Official international scholarship page and call index
sources.evidence: The University announced 30 merit scholarships of €10,000 each for eligible EU students from universities outside Italy enrolling in Master's degrees in 2026/27; the scholarship page lists an application period 5 May–15 June 2026, later extended to 26 June. The programme is limited by applicant eligibility and is not a general award to all international applicants. It does not establish a 2027/28 call.

sources.title: Regional scholarships AY 2026/27
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 Lombardy regional DSU competition was for enrolled University of Milan students meeting annual income and merit criteria; applications ran 10 July–30 September. Awards may include a cash scholarship, meal and full or partial fee exemption. International applicants with foreign income must follow the annual documentation rules. No 2027/28 call is confirmed.

sources.title: International scholarships – new Excellence award status
sources.evidence: The official award administration page states that no new allocations of the international Excellence Scholarships will be made from AY 2026/27. This does not affect separate 2026/27 European Futures or university/DSU competitions.

sources.title: Welcome Desk – International Admissions and Credentials Evaluation
sources.evidence: The University directs applicants who are not resident in Italy or hold foreign qualifications to the International Admissions and Credentials Evaluation Office through InformaStudenti. General contact route only.

sources.title: Application for international students
sources.evidence: The reviewed page lists 2026/27 application rounds and a €60 fee; values are retained only as prior-cycle context and are not copied into the active dataset.

sources.title: Admission: how it works
sources.evidence: General guidance says visa-applicant calls are program-specific and typically run December–March; it describes ranked selection, merit-based fee brackets and scholarship/accommodation procedures, but does not confirm individual 2027/28 programs.

sources.title: Pre-enrolment and study-visa application
sources.evidence: Explains visa applicants’ general procedure; not a full 2027/28 program deadline source.

sources.title: Degrees offered in English
sources.evidence: Department’s English-program directory; the 2027/28 call is the source of cycle-specific availability and dates.

sources.title: International Students Admission
sources.evidence: Describes international admission steps for first- and second-cycle courses; a reviewed guide is for 2026/27, so no 2027/28 dates are inferred.

sources.title: International admissions – AY 2026/27
sources.evidence: The page explicitly limits the pre-evaluation procedure to AY 2026/27, lists up to two program applications with a €10 fee per application, and gives category-specific calls from December 2025 through November 2026. Non-EU applicants requiring visas proceed through Universitaly after positive evaluation; the visa pre-enrolment deadline shown is 30 November 2026. These procedures and dates are prior-cycle evidence only.

sources.title: Data Science for Economics, Business and Finance – UnivPM Orienta
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 profile identifies Data Science for Finance and Economics as a curriculum within Data Science for Economics, Business and Finance (LM-DATA), fully taught in English, open access with knowledge assessment, based in Ancona. The profile describes on-site lectures; a separate annual faculty notice specifies a delivery exception for this curriculum in 2026/27. This is not a 2027/28 new-entry confirmation.

sources.title: Data Science for Economics, Business and Finance – 2026/27 catalogue
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 Faculty catalogue lists the Data Science for Economics, Business and Finance Master's with LM-56 R, LM-91 R and LM-DATA classifications, and open access. The Finance and Economics name is a curriculum of this wider MSc, not a separately listed degree.

sources.title: Entry requirements for Master's degree courses – Faculty of Economics
sources.evidence: The AY 2026/27 page lists the Data Science for Economics and Enterprises degree, including the Data Science for Finance and Economics curriculum, and states that curricular requirements and adequacy of preparation are verified for Master's applicants. Detailed curriculum and credit criteria are retained from the official prior-year regulation as historical context.

sources.title: Data Science for Economics, Business and Finance – teaching regulations 2025/26
sources.evidence: The prior-year regulation specifies a suitable first-cycle qualification, named Italian degree-class routes or curricular credits, individual preparation assessment and B2 English. It lists a threshold of 12 CFU in ICT/mathematical-statistical subjects and 12 CFU in economics/statistics/business-related sectors for applicants following the curricular-credit route. Its grade/interview provisions are specific to the 2025/26 regulation and must not be carried forward as current rules.

sources.title: Language requirements for programs taught in English
sources.evidence: The international office states that students entering English-taught programs must demonstrate English at CEFR B2 through recognized certification or accepted documentation. Program-specific acceptable evidence and exemptions must be checked in the annual course procedure.

sources.title: Teaching activity methods AY 2026/27 – Faculty of Economics
sources.evidence: The Faculty's 2026/27 notice says the Data Science for Finance and Economics curriculum's lessons are provided by streaming or asynchronously as recorded lectures; examinations and graduation sessions remain in person. This annual exception is scoped to 2026/27 and differs from the generic course profile's on-site label.

sources.title: Tuition and fees AY 2026/27
sources.evidence: The first 2026/27 installment is €156 (€140 regional tax and €16 stamp duty); later installments depend on the degree course and ISEE, which must be authorized by 5 November 2026. The amount is not a complete annual tuition quote and is not valid as a 2027/28 estimate.

sources.title: 40 scholarships for first-year open-access Master's students 2026/27
sources.evidence: The university offered 40 competitive gross awards of €2,000 for first-time enrollees in an open-access Master's in 2026/27. Eligibility included a Bachelor's result from 90/110 to 110/110 with honours and valid 2026 ISEE; the application period ran 15 July–17 November 2026. This general award was not guaranteed to any individual program and does not establish a 2027/28 call.

sources.title: ERDIS Marche scholarship call 2026/27
sources.evidence: ERDIS Marche opened its annual regional scholarship call for 2026/27 to students at Marche universities, including international students subject to the annual eligibility criteria. Online applications ran 14 July–28 August 2026; regional aid may include scholarship and student services under the call. This does not confirm 2027/28 rules or awards.

sources.title: ERDIS Marche scholarships and benefits
sources.evidence: ERDIS describes annual competitive aid for students enrolled at universities in Marche, with benefits including financial awards and possible meals/accommodation subject to eligibility and call conditions. It states that applications must be renewed each academic year.

sources.title: Useful contacts – International UnivPM
sources.evidence: The International Students' Admission Office page lists official contact channels, including the Economics-area phone number. General contact information only; the current call should be used to confirm 2027/28 procedures.

sources.title: Enrolment of non-EU students residing abroad
sources.evidence: Page gives 2026/27 application and document deadlines and does not establish 2027/28 program-level dates.

sources.title: Enrol in a post-graduate course
sources.evidence: General guidance for international applicants to postgraduate courses; no 2027/28 catalog or cycle-specific deadline is stated on this page.

sources.title: Foreign study qualification
sources.evidence: Explains foreign-qualification procedures and directs candidates to degree-specific calls; no 2027/28 catalog or deadline is established here.

sources.title: International Applications – Faculty of Engineering
sources.evidence: For foreign applicants to English-taught engineering master's programs, the teaching committee evaluates the academic career and may require a test (usually in September); non-EU applicants need a visa/pre-enrolment, and Computer Engineering applicants must accept an offer. The faculty says it accepts a limited number of non-student applicants per course and gives priority to applicants who accept offers. General faculty guidance; no course-specific 2027/28 call.

sources.title: How to apply to Master’s degree programs – 2027/28 calendar
sources.evidence: For non-restricted-access Master’s programs, the 2027/28 application windows are 12–18 Nov 2026, 12–20 Jan 2027, 12–22 Mar 2027, 6–12 Jun 2027, and 1–8 Sep 2027. In March and June, non-EU applicants abroad may apply only if spots remain; the September window is for EU and non-EU residents in Italy. The application fee is €35. Restricted-access programs have their own calls and schedules; check the program category and portal listing. These university-wide rules do not confirm Computer Engineering’s 2027/28 intake or category.

sources.title: Computer Engineering – official course profile and 2026/27 plan
sources.evidence: Lists Computer Engineering as a second-cycle degree, two years, taught entirely in English, LM-32 Computer Systems Engineering, Engineering area, Pavia, and free access. The linked study plan is explicitly for enrollment year 2026/27; this is prior-cycle course evidence and does not establish a 2027/28 first-year intake.

sources.title: Computer Engineering course regulations 2026/27
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 regulations require a recognized qualifying degree, at least 36 basic and 45 specific advanced CFU (81 total across listed subject areas), English at B2, and suitable engineering preparation. The preparation may be assessed in sessions in September–October or January–February; some applicants can be exempt from the assessment based on marks. Foreign qualifications are evaluated case by case. These criteria and dates are prior-cycle regulations, not confirmed 2027/28 conditions.

sources.title: Non-EU prospective students – 2026/27 fees
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, non-EU students can use a citizenship- and study-area-based flat rate of €390–€4,550 per year without financial documents, or submit financial documents for family-income-based fees. Applicants seeking EDiSU benefits must use the income-based route. The page links the 2026/27 fee table; no 2027/28 amounts are stated.

sources.title: Flat-rate tuition brackets 2026/27
sources.evidence: For the 2026/27 non-EU flat-rate schedule, the science-area annual amounts are €390, €1,520, or €4,550 for country brackets 1, 2, and 3. Computer Engineering is in the Engineering area. Country bracket and fee-area classification determine the applicable amount; these are not 2027/28 tuition values.

sources.title: EDiSU ordinary scholarship call 2026/27
sources.evidence: The annual 2026/27 call was open to Italian, EU and foreign students, including incoming applicants who intended to apply to Pavia; eligibility depended on income and merit, and funding determined which eligible students became beneficiaries. The 15 September 2026 deadline has passed. Amounts vary by income/geographic status; the official call gives up to €8,248 including a daily meal for eligible off-site students, with different structures for EDiSU college residents. This is regional, not Computer Engineering-specific, and does not establish a 2027/28 award.

sources.title: Financial support for international students
sources.evidence: The page describes annual EDiSU calls with possible accommodation, one meal per day and an income-based cash amount; it lists the 2026/27 call deadlines and names separate subject scholarships for Civil Engineering for Mitigation of Risk and Environmental Engineering REACH, not Computer Engineering. No dedicated Computer Engineering scholarship is identified on this page; no 2027/28 award is inferred.

sources.title: Tuition exemptions and incentives 2026/27
sources.source_type: Official fee exemption and incentive guidance
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, EDiSU scholarship beneficiaries and eligible non-beneficiaries receive automatic exemption from the all-inclusive tuition fee; equivalent ISEE up to €32,000 also qualifies for full all-inclusive-fee exemption. The page lists a €450 incentive under 2025/26 rules for selected classes including LM-32, but that prior-year award is not a 2026/27 or 2027/28 promise. No 2027/28 rules are stated.

sources.title: Engineering degree catalogue 2026/27
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 Department of Engineering catalogue lists Engineering Management as an English-taught three-year L-8 R/L-9 R Bachelor’s and a two-year LM-31 Master’s in Perugia. It also lists other engineering degrees whose teaching is Italian or mixed English/Italian. The catalogue is prior-cycle evidence and does not confirm either course's 2027/28 first-year intake.

sources.title: Engineering Management – First cycle degree course
sources.evidence: The page, last updated 19 October 2026, describes the three-year English BSc, a sustainable capacity of 180 students, a school-leaving qualification, B2 English, and a mandatory basic-knowledge assessment. It lists TOLC-I, SAT and ACT guidance and OFA rules. The current page does not establish a 2027/28 call or intake.

sources.title: Engineering Management – Second cycle degree course
sources.evidence: The page, last updated 19 October 2026, describes the English 120-ECTS two-year LM-31 MSc, 80 sustainable places, direct access for L-8/L-9 graduates, an 85-CFU curricular route for other backgrounds, B2 English, committee review of foreign qualifications, and course enrollment guidance. These are current/prior-cycle course details, not a 2027/28 admission call.

sources.title: Tuition Fees and scholarships – 2026/27 guidance
sources.evidence: The page, last updated 6 October 2026, says exact 2026/27 fees are governed by the University Regulation and gives a usual annual range of €150–€2,200 depending on family income and merit. Applicants whose family income/assets are abroad may use a four-bracket country-based flat contribution or opt for ISEEU Parificato; low-human-development-country and protection-status rules also apply. It does not publish 2027/28 fees.

sources.title: ADiSU Umbria scholarship and services call 2026/27
sources.evidence: The regional 2026/27 call was open to students enrolled or intending to enroll at Umbria institutions, subject to income, enrollment and merit requirements. The published application deadline was 2 September 2026 at noon. ISEE and ISPE limits were €28,339.88 and €61,608.48. Applicants with foreign household income/assets had to submit supporting foreign-income documentation by separate deadlines (2 September or 30 October 2026), following legalization/translation rules. These regional benefits are competitive and are not a program-specific guaranteed award; no 2027/28 call is confirmed.

sources.title: ADiSU Umbria 2026/27 scholarship call – official PDF
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 call publishes cash amounts by ISEE band and student status plus meal/accommodation values. In the lowest-income band, maximum standard totals include €8,246.78 for an off-site student with paid lodging (cash plus two daily meals), €8,246.78 for an off-site student in an ADiSU bed (cash, bed and meals), €4,819.32 for a commuter (cash plus one daily meal), and €3,623.68 for an in-town student (cash plus one daily meal). Award amounts reduce by income band and depend on eligibility, ranking, service allocation and documentation. Annex 4 lists Engineering Management BSc course L0615 (L-8/L-9) and MSc course M0622 (LM-31) among STEM courses eligible for a 20% cash uplift for women; this uplift is subject to the call's other rules and is not a guaranteed award. This is 2026/27 evidence only.

sources.title: How to apply
sources.evidence: States that annual rules, deadlines and tests are listed in the prospectus published each June; non-EU applicants follow pre-enrolment and course-level reserved-place procedures.

sources.title: International degree-seeking students
sources.evidence: Reviewed page states 2026/27 international master's call status; it does not confirm 2027/28 program availability or deadlines.

sources.title: Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine – course profile
sources.evidence: The profile identifies a two-year Master's degree, class LM-6 R, taught in English in Verona, with limited entry by qualifications. The displayed profile is for 2026/27 and does not establish a 2027/28 first-year intake.

sources.title: Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine – 2026/27 admissions
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, the course page lists 35 total places, 5 reserved for specified non-EU applicants, qualification-based selection, applications 1 July–31 August 2026 by 10:00 Italian time, first ranking on 18 September 2026 and a €50 admission fee. These are prior-cycle values.

sources.title: Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine – admission requirements
sources.evidence: The reviewed page is for 2026/27. It describes qualifying biology/biotechnology and other degree classes or specified science credits, an English B2 requirement with listed exemptions, and a separate set of criteria for applicants with degrees earned abroad; it does not confirm 2027/28 requirements.

sources.title: International admission call – Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine, 2026/27
sources.evidence: Separate 2026/27 call for applicants with a foreign degree, non-Italian citizenship and no residence in Italy: 5 reserved places; relevant first-level degree; weighted CGPA above 81%; English B2 or a prior English-taught qualification; application 2 February–31 March 2026 at 15:00 Italian time; €50 pre-admission fee. It also lists one €8,000 gross/year scholarship with tuition exemption and four €1,000 flat-rate contributions for two academic years. This is historical evidence and must not be added to or assumed for 2027/28.

sources.title: Biology for Translational Research and Precision Medicine – 2026/27 cohort study plan
sources.evidence: The study plan for students enrolled in 2026/27 says the second year will activate in 2027/28. This confirms planned second-year teaching for that cohort only and is not a new-entry admission notice.

sources.title: Master’s degrees – international English course list
sources.evidence: Lists two-year, 120-credit master’s degrees and identifies Chemistry, Computer Science (4 curricula), Mathematics and Applications (2 curricula named Advanced Theoretical Mathematics and Applied Engineering Oriented Mathematics), and Physics as English-taught. The page does not specify an academic year, so it supports discovery and course identity only, not a 2027/28 first-year intake.

sources.title: Manifesto degli studi – academic offer and regulations 2026/27
sources.evidence: The official study-manifesto page identifies the 2026/27 academic offer and regulations and links the annual manifesto, course offer and student-benefit documents. It is a prior-cycle source and does not establish 2027/28 new-entry availability.

sources.title: Computer Science – official degree profile
sources.evidence: Identifies Computer Science as an English-taught LM-18 Master’s in Camerino, two years/120 CFU and open access. The profile names four active curricula (AI, SDT, BIS and MTDC) but later says the course has five curricula; the separate international English master list also says four. This profile does not itself specify an academic year or confirm 2027/28 intake.

sources.title: Master’s Degree in Chemistry – official English degree profile
sources.evidence: Identifies a two-year, 120-credit LM-54 Master’s degree in Chemistry in Camerino, with training activities delivered in English. The international English master list also uses Chemistry, while the Italian School page and 2026/27 international package retain the title Chemistry and Advanced Chemical Methodologies; the official materials use both titles. This does not confirm 2027/28 intake.

sources.title: Chemistry and Advanced Chemical Methodologies – official course page
sources.evidence: The Italian School of Chemistry page identifies Chemistry and Advanced Chemical Methodologies as an LM-54, two-year, 120-CFU course in Camerino and says all educational activities are delivered in English. This differs from the shorter Chemistry title used on the English profile and international English master list; confirm the preferred displayed title in the 2027/28 offer.

sources.title: Mathematics and Applications – official degree profile
sources.evidence: Identifies Mathematics and Applications as an English-taught LM-40 Master’s in Camerino, two years/120 CFU and open access. It lists three curricula (Pure Mathematics, Mathematics for Industrial Engineering, Mathematics for Analytics and Finance) and says entry requires a Mathematics bachelor’s or another bachelor’s with at least 30 ECTS in Mathematics plus adequate Algebra, Analysis and Geometry; English B1 is required. The international master list instead says two curricula with different names. This does not confirm 2027/28 intake.

sources.title: Physics – official degree profile
sources.evidence: Identifies Physics as an English-taught LM-17 Master’s in Camerino, two years/120 CFU and open access. Entry requires a first-level degree or foreign equivalent with at least 70 CFU in Physics subject areas and 30 CFU in Mathematics and Informatics; English B1 is required. The profile is general/current and does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

sources.title: Pre-admissions 2026/27 – international applicants
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, the non-EU pre-admission call is closed and the listed deadline was 31 March 2026; EU/equivalent non-visa applicants are directed to welcome@unicam.it. International candidates register in the teaching portal, submit preliminary curriculum evaluation and pay a non-refundable €20 fee. For English courses Cambridge, IELTS or TOEFL documents are optional at pre-admission and MOI certificates are excluded by this page; a positive evaluation is not final enrolment and visa applicants must continue through Universitaly. No 2027/28 route or deadline is confirmed.

sources.title: Pre-admission procedure – official guide 2026/27
sources.evidence: The guide describes registration, preliminary evaluation and document upload for 2026/27 BSc, MSc and one-tier MSc applicants; mandatory documents and completed €20 payment were required before committee evaluation. It is historical process evidence and does not establish a 2027/28 application route or deadline.

sources.title: Fees for foreign students
sources.evidence: The page describes income-based ISEE-U equalised assessment for specified foreign applicants, fixed annual fees of €200 for students from designated particularly poor/developing countries and €300 for non-OECD countries outside that list, with regional tax and stamp duty added. It also describes a €6,876 all-inclusive option. The page does not label these amounts with an academic year; do not treat them as 2027/28 fees.

sources.title: Lump-sum enrollment package for international MSc students 2026/27
sources.source_type: Official international tuition and accommodation offer
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, the University advertised five places per named two-year MSc, including Chemistry and Advanced Chemical Methodologies, Computer Science, Mathematics and Applications, and Physics. The package costs €6,876 per academic year and includes tuition, double-room accommodation October–July, two meals per day while the canteen is open, local bus, sports facilities and administrative support, payable in four instalments. Historical offer only; no 2027/28 package is confirmed.

sources.title: University tuition and student contributions 2026/27
sources.evidence: The University fee page publishes 2026/27 contribution rules and installment details. Amounts depend on ISEE-U and other eligibility conditions; its all-inclusive domestic offer is not treated as an international flat rate. No 2027/28 fee schedule was identified.

sources.title: ERDIS Marche scholarship call service – 2026/27
sources.source_type: Official regional scholarship service and call page
sources.evidence: ERDIS identifies Italian and foreign students at Camerino and other Marche universities as eligible to apply subject to merit and financial criteria. The 2026/27 deadline was 28 August 2026; applications are annual and online, and awards may include cash, meals, accommodation and tuition/tax exemptions. No 2027/28 call is confirmed.

sources.title: WELCOMEINUNICAM scholarships for two-year Master’s students 2026/27
sources.evidence: The University announced 30 WELCOMEINUNICAM awards of €1,500 each for first-time entrants with an Italian or foreign bachelor’s degree enrolling in year one of a two-year MSc in 2026/27. The application deadline was 18 February 2027 at 12:00 through the student portal. This is a prior-cycle notice, not a 2027/28 award commitment.

sources.title: Degree catalogue 2026/27
sources.evidence: The catalogue page identifies the 2026/27 offer and lists bachelor's and master's degrees, including the two-year, English-taught Physics MSc (LM-17). It is an annual prior-cycle catalogue and does not establish new-entry availability for 2027/28.

sources.title: Physics – course profile 2026/27
sources.evidence: The official profile names Physics as a Laurea Magistrale in class LM-17, at Ferrara, with open access and English teaching for academic year 2026/27; it also notes a double-degree option. This confirms course identity in the prior-cycle catalogue only.

sources.title: Physics – degree overview
sources.evidence: The course page says the Physics master's is fully taught in English, awards 120 ECTS over two years, and is the natural follow-up to a bachelor's degree in Physics or a related area. It is general course information and does not confirm a 2027/28 intake.

sources.title: Physics – admission and enrolment guidance, 2026/27
sources.evidence: The course page identifies an extra-EU 2026/27 enrolment period of 12 January–30 April. Applicants need a Physics bachelor's degree, Italian L-30 or legacy class 25 degree, or a certified foreign bachelor's degree; the committee evaluates the academic record and Physics background through an interview that also checks English skills. The listed background includes calculus, geometry, algebra, chemistry, core classical and modern physics, experimental methods, electronics and computing. No 2027/28 course-specific dates or intake are established.

sources.title: Apply for a Master's degree – international procedure
sources.evidence: For the 2026/27 cycle, non-EU applicants abroad applying to Physics were directed to submit through apply.unife.it from 12 January to 30 April, pay a non-refundable €20 application fee, upload qualification documents and also submit through Universitaly. ER.GO scholarship/accommodation applications are normally announced in July and August. This page was last updated 4 June 2026 and does not establish the 2027/28 route, fee or dates.

sources.title: Applicants with foreign qualifications – applicant categories
sources.evidence: For extra-EU applicants resident abroad applying to English-taught Physics, the page specifies apply.unife.it registration from 12 January to 30 April and Universitaly pre-enrolment by 30 June. It also says course-specific reserved places are set annually and evaluation requires applications through both systems. The page was last updated 18 December 2025; these dates are recorded as the prior-cycle route only.

sources.title: Entrance visa request – international students
sources.evidence: Updated 25 May 2026. For the 2026/27 process, non-EU applicants abroad apply through Universitaly; admission/pre-enrolment does not guarantee a study visa. The page states an English certificate of at least B2 may be required by the relevant embassy/consulate when English is not the applicant's mother tongue, and students must complete enrolment in Ferrara within one month of visa issuance (31 January only for late-issued visas). It does not establish a 2027/28 visa procedure.

sources.title: University fees and contribution rules, 2026/27
sources.source_type: Official annual fees and contribution page
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 contribution page uses ISEE or foreign-income documentation and study-year/credit rules. First-year students with ISEE up to €27,000 receive a full tuition-contribution exemption and pay €156 in stamp and regional tax; the listed contribution at ISEE above €60,000 or without ISEE is €2,092 for regular first-year students. These amounts depend on eligibility and are prior-cycle only, not a 2027/28 international flat fee.

sources.title: ISEE or foreign-income documentation for fees
sources.evidence: The University allows students with income abroad to request a fee reduction using the required foreign-income documentation instead of ISEE. The page says the 2026/27 deadline was 2 November 2026, with a €100 surcharge for documentation submitted from 3 November to 15 December 2026. Annual deadline and fee rules do not establish 2027/28 terms.

sources.title: ER.GO study-benefit competition call 2026/27
sources.source_type: Official regional scholarship and student-benefit call
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 regional call includes students enrolling at the University of Ferrara in bachelor's and master's degrees. Foreign students are eligible subject to income, merit and documentation conditions; benefits can include a scholarship, accommodation and meals, and application/award terms are governed by the annual call. This is prior-cycle regional aid and does not confirm a 2027/28 award or deadline.

sources.title: International Mobility Office – contact information
sources.source_type: Official university international office contact page
sources.evidence: Lists international@unife.it as the contact for incoming international mobility and student-support activities. It is a general contact, not a 2027/28 admissions decision channel.

sources.title: Physics – teaching manager contact
sources.evidence: Names Anca Teodora Lazar as the Physics degree's didactic manager and gives manager.fisica@unife.it as the course contact. This is a course-information contact, not a 2027/28 intake confirmation.

sources.title: Informatica (Computer Science) – official course profile 2026/27
sources.evidence: The current course profile lists Informatica (Computer Science) as a two-year Laurea Magistrale in Varese, English-taught and open access. The page links the 2026/27 course regulation and SUA-CdS and repeats the current course entry requirements. The profile does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

sources.title: Informatica MSc course regulation 2026/27
sources.evidence: The official 2026/27 regulation identifies Informatica as an LM-18, two-year Laurea Magistrale based in Varese, with English teaching and open access. It is prior-cycle evidence and does not establish 2027/28 availability.

sources.title: Admission requirements – Informatica
sources.evidence: Applicants may hold an Italian L-31/26 or L-8/09 bachelor’s degree; other or foreign degrees can qualify with at least 60 CFU in INF-01/A and IINF-05/A combined and 18 CFU in the specified mathematics sectors. English at B2 or equivalent is required, and all applicants undergo an interview on fundamental computer science; a negative interview result bars access for that academic year. The page reflects the current/2026/27 requirements and is not a 2027/28 notice.

sources.title: Pre-enrolment for non-single-cycle Master's degrees, 2026/27
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, pre-enrolment to open-access MSc courses ran from 1 July to 30 October 2026 via Student Web Services/Esse3, using the 'Test di valutazione' application and supporting identity and qualification documents. The course secretariat evaluates the qualifications and contacts the applicant for an interview; eligible students then complete enrolment and pay through PagoPA. The next-cycle calendar is not stated.

sources.title: Enrolment for non-EU students resident abroad
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, applicants needing a study visa had to apply for pre-enrolment and preliminary assessment through Universitaly, with submissions accepted through 30 June 2026. University guidance describes foreign-qualification documentation and says applicants to English-taught courses are exempt from the University's Italian-language test. These are annual prior-cycle procedures, not 2027/28 deadlines.

sources.title: Student contribution regulation 2026/27
sources.source_type: Official annual tuition and contribution regulation
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 regulation sets the registration payment at €146 initially, composed of €16 stamp duty and €130 regional tax, with possible regional-tax adjustment to €160 or €190 based on ISEE. For regular students in Area B (the area including Informatica), the university contribution is zero up to €28,000 ISEE and reaches €3,660 above €66,000. Students with foreign citizenship and family income/assets abroad may instead use a country-group flat contribution; for Area B's K=1.1 coefficient, the 2026/27 amounts are €220, €770 or €3,630 by group. Rules depend on eligibility and are historical only; no 2027/28 schedule was identified.

sources.title: Merit and excellence scholarships under the 2026/27 fee regulation
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 contribution regulation lists university-wide merit awards for two-year MSc students: 15 first-year in-residence awards of €2,000, 7 first-year out-of-residence awards of €3,000, and 20 second-year awards of €750. Awards are competitive, subject to the regulation and its eligibility conditions, and do not guarantee an award to Computer Science applicants or confirm a 2027/28 call.

sources.title: Right-to-study benefits call 2026/27
sources.source_type: Official regional DSU scholarship and accommodation call
sources.evidence: The annual call offers competitive right-to-study benefits including scholarships/meal support and reduced-rate accommodation, subject to financial and merit criteria. In 2026/27 scholarship/meal applications ran 24 July–30 September 2026 and accommodation applications 24 July–24 August; foreign students could use ISEE Parificato procedures. No 2027/28 call is identified.

sources.title: Scholarships and right-to-study support
sources.evidence: The University describes regional-funded right-to-study scholarships as competitive and jointly dependent on merit, academic progression and income; amounts vary by income band and travel distance and are set in the annual call. A separate university merit-scholarship page links awards for BSc and single-cycle students; that page is not treated as a Computer Science MSc award source.

sources.title: Infostudenti – student information and contact service
sources.evidence: The course profile and university service directory link Infostudenti as the student information/contact pathway. No verified course-specific admissions email is published on the reviewed course profile; the contact pathway is provided instead of inferring an email address.

sources.title: Computer Science – official course sheet 2026/27
sources.evidence: The official course sheet identifies Computer Science as a two-year LM-18 Master's in L'Aquila, taught in English, with open admission subject to assessment of personal competencies and skills. It is prior-cycle evidence and does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

sources.title: Computer Science LM-18 teaching regulations 2026/27
sources.evidence: Article 5 lists L-31/legacy class 26 or another qualifying degree with 48 CFU in INF-01/A or IINF-05/A and 12 CFU in the named mathematics sectors, and written/oral English at B2. The regulation describes the 2026/27 curriculum; required courses are in English while some optional courses may be in Italian. Prior-cycle criteria only.

sources.title: Selection call for international Master's applicants, cohort 2026
sources.evidence: The foreign-degree selection call for 2026/27 included Computer Science. It required a foreign Bachelor's degree of at least three years, B2 English (with an accepted certificate less than four years old or stated exemptions), and applied through PICA by 25 February 2026 at 13:00 Italy time with a €20 fee. Applicants could select up to two course rankings. The call is closed prior-cycle evidence; after selection, visa applicants were directed to Universitaly.

sources.title: International degree courses 2026/27
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 official English international-degree catalogue lists Computer Science as a two-year second-cycle LM-18 course. The catalogue is prior-cycle evidence and does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

sources.title: Tuition and student contributions 2026/27
sources.evidence: For 2026/27 the fixed initial payment was €156 (regional tax plus stamp duty); the annual COA varied with household income/ISEE and other eligibility conditions. The page set the ISEE authorization deadline at 20 December 2026 and payment dates through January–May 2027. These are historical annual rules, not 2027/28 tuition values.

sources.title: Student contribution FAQ – international student provisions
sources.evidence: The FAQ explains that students with foreign family income may request equivalent ISEE; specified low-human-development-country students with a foreign entry qualification, refugees, Italian-government scholarship recipients, joint/multiple-degree students and ADSU scholarship recipients may qualify to pay the €156 fixed amount under the stated conditions. Recheck the annual fee guide for 2027/28 eligibility and values.

sources.title: Calls for international students 2026/27
sources.source_type: Official international scholarships and admissions calls index
sources.evidence: The University's 2026/27 index lists the foreign-degree English-Master's admission call, the ADSU residence call and 50 contributions toward travel and installation costs for foreign students intending to enroll in English-taught Master's programs. The published deadlines were 25 February, 27 July and 9 July 2026 respectively. No 2027/28 calls are established by this page.

sources.title: Travel and installation contributions for international Master's students 2026/27
sources.source_type: Official international student grant call index
sources.evidence: The University listed 50 competitive contributions to student travel and installation costs for foreign students intending to enroll in English-taught Master's programs in 2026/27, with a 9 July 2026 deadline. The index does not publish an amount in the reviewed summary and does not establish an award for new 2027/28 entrants.

sources.title: UNICORE 8.0 scholarship call 2026/27
sources.evidence: The targeted call offered one scholarship for an eligible refugee student residing in a listed country to enter an English-taught second-cycle degree, including Computer Science, in 2026/27. It described €4,800 per year from the University and additional partner benefits, with renewal into 2027/28 subject to merit. This is not a general scholarship or a new 2027/28-entry award.

sources.title: ADSU L'Aquila scholarship call 2026/27
sources.evidence: ADSU published its annual 2026/27 competitive scholarship call for students at the University of L'Aquila and other local institutions. The application deadline was 31 August 2026. This is general regional student aid subject to the annual call and eligibility rules; it is not a guaranteed Computer Science award or a 2027/28 call.

sources.title: ADSU L'Aquila student residence call 2026/27
sources.evidence: The regional agency's 2026/27 residence call awarded student beds through an online competition, with a 27 July 2026 deadline. The call is annual and does not establish a 2027/28 housing or scholarship offer.

sources.title: Computer Science international admissions ranking 2026/27
sources.evidence: The University published the list of candidates eligible to enroll in the English-taught Computer Science Master's program for 2026/27. The list is an outcome for one call and does not provide a complete applicant denominator or an acceptance rate.

sources.title: UniGe degree course catalogue
sources.evidence: The catalogue links the ten reviewed BSc/MSc candidates to course profiles displaying Info 2026/2027. Separate Computer Engineering BSc records exist for Italian teaching in Genoa (11880) and English teaching in Imperia (12133). No named 2027/28 first-year offer is established by this catalogue.

sources.title: UniGeApply international admissions 2026/27
sources.evidence: For non-Italian qualifications, UniGeApply was the initial assessment route. Visa applicants: 26 November 2025–20 March 2026, €30 fixed for up to two requests; Computer Engineering BSc closed early on 8 March 2026. Resident selection opened 9 April 2026 and closed 28 August for MSc or 25 September for BSc, subject to restricted-course exceptions, and was free. Successful visa candidates continued via Universitaly. These are 2026/27 dates only.

sources.title: How tuition fees work – 2026/27
sources.evidence: Three installments: initial €136 consists of €16 stamp and €120 minimum regional tax, with any tax adjustment later. University contribution depends on ISEE-U, fee class, study group and full/part-time enrollment; the full-time table ranges from €0 to €3,300 plus fixed charges. 2026/27 deadlines: first installment 5 October for BSc or 30 November for open-access MSc, second 10 December 2026, third 23 June 2027. €136 is not total annual tuition.

sources.title: ISEE-University and equivalent ISEE – 2026/27
sources.evidence: For 2026/27, income-based fees use ISEE-U; eligible foreign household-income cases use equivalent ISEE-U parificato. Ordinary DSU/self-certification deadline is 31 October 2026. The page gives late DSU charges of €100 through 30 November and €200 from 1 December through 15 June 2027. Verify annual documentation and eligibility rather than assuming the lowest tuition bracket.

sources.title: UniGe university fee benefits
sources.evidence: Current guidance describes a €200 first-year contribution reduction for the highest entry-qualification mark and later-year merit reductions of €400 or €200, subject to the fee regulations. ALiSEO scholarship winners have university contribution and regional-tax exemptions. These rules do not establish a new 2027/28 scholarship call.

sources.title: ALiSEO scholarship and accommodation call 2026/27
sources.evidence: Annual competitive benefits require enrollment, merit and economic eligibility; ISEE/ISEEUP must not exceed €28,339 and ISPEU/ISPEUP €61,608. Awards vary by income band and on-site/commuting/off-site classification, with cash, meal and possible housing components. In band 1A an off-site housing applicant's €7,172 gross award includes services rather than all cash. Foreign-income applicants require the call's equivalent-ISEE documentation. No 2027/28 award is inferred.

sources.title: ALiSEO 2026/27 call instructions
sources.evidence: The 2026/27 scholarship/housing application window was 15 June–31 July 2026 at 12:00. The page says the deadline has passed. Foreign applicants without an Italian identity document have a separate registration procedure. This is a closed prior-cycle competition.

sources.title: UniGe Welcome Office – international students
sources.evidence: The Welcome Office contact is sass@unige.it; call centre 010 33 55 000, dial 4. The page links international-enrollment, support and appointment services. It also describes targeted 2026/27 Palestinian-student scholarships; these are not general international awards.

sources.title: Computer Engineering BSc Imperia – ATHENA assessment
sources.evidence: ATHENA is a non-selective computing/mathematics initial assessment; weak results lead to OFA. The English section is compulsory without an accepted B2 certificate. Dates run September 2026–January 2027; the 20 November assessment was moved to 4 December 2026. The 22 January 2027 date is reserved for non-EU students arriving from December onward.

sources.title: Computer Science BSc – initial preparation assessment
sources.evidence: The course uses TE.L.E.MA.CO. for initial preparation assessment. Foreign school-qualification holders follow Italian-language verification and remedial guidance. This course page is not a 2027/28 admission call.

sources.title: Computer Engineering MSc – personal readiness assessment
sources.evidence: Applicants submit degree/transcripts, CV and B2 English evidence, with accepted English-medium or degree-exam alternatives or CLAT testing. Foreign-applicant assessment uses documented preparation scoring with admission at 85/110; foreign candidates without B1 Italian may add an Italian-language exam to the study plan. This undated guidance does not establish the 2027/28 procedure.

sources.title: Computer Science MSc – course profile 2026/27
sources.evidence: The official profile displays 2026/2027: Computer Science, MSc, 2 years/120 ECTS, class LM-18, English, Genoa, In-person. It describes free access subject to the course's entry/initial or personal preparation checks. This verifies the previous-cycle listing only.

sources.evidence: degree: Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS; curriculum: At least 50% of credits in computer science, computer engineering, mathematics, physics or statistics; english: B2; the page's certificate clauses still explicitly refer to 2024/25 and 2025/26; assessment: Interview in computing and mathematics, potentially preceded by a quiz. Reviewed alongside the 2026/27 profile; no 2027/28 course call is established.

sources.evidence: Official inventory is explicitly AY 2026-2027; Computer Engineering LM-32 is an Italian-language open-access Master. No 2027/28 course offer is established.

sources.title: Computer Engineering MSc – course 20-362
sources.evidence: Course profile identifies a two-year, Italian-language, open-access LM-32 Master in Modena. President Francesco Guerra, francesco.guerra@unimore.it.

sources.title: Computer Engineering MSc admission call 2026/27
sources.evidence: Assessment deadline 14 December 2026; enrollment 8 July–22 December 2026. Academic requirements, foreign-degree assessment, 10 reserved non-EU abroad places, Italian language and ESSE3/Universitaly steps are specified. The call provides no acceptance-rate denominator or specific application fee.

sources.title: Computer Engineering – department information
sources.evidence: Department describes Cloud and Cyber Security and Data Engineering and Analytics tracks since 2023/24. General entry description mentions degree score at least 85/110 or foreign score above three quarters; the annual course call controls admission.

sources.title: Foreign study qualification
sources.evidence: Foreign qualification guidance directs open-access MSc applicants to ESSE3 academic assessment and the individual annual call; visa applicants also pre-enrol through Universitaly. Bachelor admission requires a recognized school qualification after at least 12 years. Translation/legalization and DOV/CIMEA documentation apply as required.

sources.title: Fees and benefits 2026/27
sources.evidence: First-year initial fixed payment is €159.67, with any variable contribution charged later. Normal payments are up to four installments; first-year open-access MSc first and second installments are due 22 December 2026, then 1 March and 30 April 2027.

sources.title: Student fee resolution – 14 May 2026
sources.evidence: 2026/27 fee resolution sets Computer Engineering MSc maximum annual fees including fixed items at €2,290 (€2,540 for the specified fuori-corso category). Fixed items total €159.67. ISEE/merit reductions and optional foreign-income country-ISEE flat tax are regulated separately.

sources.title: Flat Tax Non-EU International Students
sources.evidence: Optional country-based notional ISEE for non-EU students resident abroad with income and assets abroad. Applicants may instead submit translated/legalized financial documents. Links a 2026/27 country table and simulator; no 2027/28 rate is established.

sources.title: No Tax Area / ISEE reductions
sources.evidence: 2026/27 No Tax Area and reduced contributions depend on ISEE and, after the first year, merit. First-year Master applicants apply via ER.GO by 22 December 2026 at 16:00. The fixed €159.67 remains payable for qualifying exemptions.

sources.title: Top Student exemption 2026/27
sources.evidence: Conditional first-year fee exemption scheme requires top prior qualification marks; MSc applicants need 110/110. Outside Emilia-Romagna residents pay fixed €159.67 only; region residents pay €859.67 total. MSc application deadline 22 December 2026 at 16:00. Foreign-grade equivalence is not specified on this page.

sources.title: ER.GO 2026/27 study-benefit competition
sources.evidence: Regional annual competition covers UNIMORE students. Scholarship application: 23 June–24 August 2026 16:00. Cash/services depend on income, merit and residence classification. Example lowest income band: off-site €7,171.11, commuting €4,190.71, on-site €2,890.16, including any meal-service conversion; higher ISEE reduces amounts. Foreign financial documentation is required.

sources.title: ER.GO economic thresholds 2026/27
sources.evidence: Scholarship and housing economic thresholds: ISEE ≤€25,000 and ISPE ≤€50,000. Both indicators must qualify; other benefits have separate thresholds.

sources.title: International Welcome Desk (Modena)
sources.evidence: International Welcome Desk: internationalwelcomedesk@unimore.it, telephone 059 2058171, Via San Geminiano 3, Modena.

sources.title: Computer Engineering BSc call 2026/27
sources.evidence: BSc Computer Engineering has a separate 2026/27 call, published 11 March 2026. The catalogue classifies the Modena BSc as Italian and restricted access. This BSc is not the existing legacy MSc candidate.

sources.title: Degree offer 2026/27
sources.evidence: Lists Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, LM-18, Palermo, open access. The university resolution sets a general non-EU-abroad capacity of 30 for conventional open-access courses; the course row does not give a separate quota. This is a 2026/27 offer.

sources.title: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence – new-enrolment study plan
sources.evidence: The new-enrolment study plan is explicitly labelled 2026/2027, with 2025/2026 in the archive. It does not publish a 2027/28 first-year plan.

sources.title: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence – course profile
sources.evidence: Names the LM-18 MSc in Palermo and course contact cicsi@unipa.it. Lists B2 English and entry via L-31, L-35, L-8, L-41 or L-30 degrees, another Italian degree with 6 ECTS Mathematics/Physics and 12 ECTS Computing, or an equivalent foreign degree. The profile has no 2027/28 intake declaration.

sources.title: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence – course presentation
sources.evidence: The course presentation explicitly identifies English as the official teaching language and English thesis writing. This is an undated programme description and cannot establish a new 2027/28 intake.

sources.title: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence – teaching regulation, 2025/26
sources.evidence: Regulation covers the 2025/26 cohort: LM-18, English, conventional teaching in Palermo. It repeats the course-profile academic routes and B2 English; candidates without L-31 must undergo a Mathematics/Computing interview with the coordinator or teachers. This regulation is not a 2026/27 or 2027/28 call.

sources.title: Giovanni Pilato – official teaching assignments
sources.evidence: Lists Information Retrieval and Natural Language Processing, 6 ECTS, under Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence in AY 2027/28. It is a teaching assignment and contains no new-entry admission, first-year cohort or application call.

sources.title: International Master degrees – 2026/27
sources.evidence: The international catalogue is labelled enrolling in AY 2026/27 and lists Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence. The page describes two-year second-cycle courses with 120 credits.

sources.title: International Students Enrolment
sources.evidence: International qualification holders use the dedicated international admission routes. Credential Evaluation Office email is internationalstudents@unipa.it. Visa pre-enrolment does not guarantee a visa.

sources.title: Extra-EU international enrolment – 2026/27
sources.evidence: For 2026/27 English MSc applications: first call 15 January–15 March; second 15 April–20 July 2026; Universitaly application by 23 August for candidates already applying in UniPa portal; personal-knowledge interviews through 30 November. Requires passport, photo, degree, transcript, language evidence and CV. English route uses UniPa portal assessment followed by Universitaly.

sources.title: First international Master call, 2026/27
sources.evidence: University notice dated 15 January 2026 gives the first Master application call as 15 January–15 March 2026 and expressly says there is no application fee for that call.

sources.title: EU and equivalent foreign-degree enrolment
sources.evidence: EU/equivalent applicants use the UniPa Student Portal. After the admission letter, the course coordinator conducts a personal-knowledge interview, including English assessment. Foreign qualifications require original legalised degree and DOV or accepted CIMEA/Diploma Supplement alternatives.

sources.title: International language requirements
sources.evidence: General guidance lists IELTS Academic 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72, PTE 46, Trinity ISE II–IV and recognised Cambridge/British Institutes qualifications. Its explicit English-certificate exemption is for programmes with a recognised English standardised admission test; it does not repeat the MOI alternative found on the 2026/27 Extra-EU page. No 2027/28 course-specific standard is established.

sources.title: International tuition fees – 2026/27 framework
sources.evidence: Foreign-resident non-EU students may choose €211/€267/€378 flat charges by country grouping or income assessment through ISEE parificato. The income route has €156 fixed charges (€140 regional tax + €16 stamp) plus a variable contribution. The flat-charge text incorrectly calls all €156 regional tax; the separate contribution table confirms €140 + €16. Financial-document references are for 2024 income and 2026 household/property circumstances.

sources.title: Student contribution table, 2026/27
sources.evidence: The table expressly covers 2026/27 and shows €16 stamp + €140 regional tax. Scientific-area contribution is €370–€2,914 by ISEE before exemptions/reductions. It gives 40%/30%/30% instalments and second-instalment deadline 29 December 2026, whereas the university web fee guide says 31 December.

sources.title: Student fees and contributions
sources.evidence: Fees comprise stamp, regional tax and income/course-dependent contribution. General schedule is 40% on enrolment, 30% by 31 December 2026 and 30% by 28 February 2027; open-access MSc pays its first instalment when enrolling. The second instalment date conflicts with the 29 December date in the 2026/27 table.

sources.title: Student contribution regulation and archive
sources.evidence: The latest table is labelled 2026/27. The linked regulation is labelled 2025/26 in force for 2026/27, but its PDF title and text are 2024/25. This document-label discrepancy should be verified before treating its exemption rules as current. No 2027/28 table appears.

sources.title: Scholarships for International Students
sources.evidence: The page lists ERSU and MAECI as 2026/27 schemes, targeted UNICORE 8.0 for refugee entrants 2026/28, and other older or restricted awards. ERSU is income/merit based and may provide tuition relief, accommodation, meals and cash. No general 2027/28 scholarship call was found.

sources.title: ERSU Palermo scholarship and services call, 2026/27
sources.evidence: Annual 2026/27 benefit competition: applications 5 June–22 July 2026 at 14:00. Income limits ISEE €23,000 and ISPE €52,500. International applicants need equivalent ISEE and residence documentation, regularisable by 30 November 2026. Monetary amounts depend on ISEE and residence classification; meals/housing values are deducted when provided. For ISEE €11,500–€15,333.33, the off-site gross base is €7,171.11; with both services the cash portion is €4,271.11. Eligibility, merit and available funding apply.

sources.title: Student contribution regulation – linked PDF dated 2024/25
sources.evidence: The regulation's decree and text expressly state AY 2024/25. The current index labels this link as a 2025/26 regulation in force for 2026/27, creating a document-label mismatch. The PDF alone cannot confirm next-cycle exemptions.

sources.evidence: Department page dated 1 September 2026 describes Sustainable Coastal and Ocean Engineering and Aerospace Engineering MSc courses as offered in English; central Aerospace profile instead says Italian/English.

sources.evidence: Current page links 2026/27 course calls and a national circular valid for 2026/27 and 2027/28. Its own Universitaly deadline is explicitly 15 September 2026; university pre-enrollment approval does not guarantee a consular visa.

sources.title: How to apply – students with foreign qualifications 2026/27
sources.evidence: Prior-cycle guide requires at least 12 school years for bachelor entry and a relevant first-cycle degree for MSc entry.
